definition_zh: 专攻；专门从事；专门研究；特化
definition_en: to concentrate on one particular subject, skill, or kind of work instead of many
core_image: 一条大道走到岔口，人只拐进其中一条窄路，越走越深
scene: 一位年轻医生放弃了全科，把全部时间投进心脏外科。A young doctor gave up general practice and specialised in heart surgery.
sceneCN: 这里 specialise 是「专门从事、专攻」（第 1 个义项：集中精力于某一领域）；句意：一位年轻医生放弃了全科，把全部时间投进心脏外科。

pos.zh: 专攻；专门从事；专门研究；特化

collocations.zh: 为本地市场做专门化调整

derivatives.zh: special + -ist 表示人，义为「专家；专科医生」
specialise + -ation 表示过程或结果，义为「专业化；专门化」
过去分词转为形容词，义为「专门的；专业化的」
与 specialty 同源，义为「专业；特产」

senses.title: To focus on one field of study or work
senses.definition: to study or research one subject in depth rather than many subjects broadly
senses.definitionCN: 深入钻研某一门学科，而不是广泛涉猎许多门
senses.example: She specialised in medieval history at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学专攻中世纪史。
senses.why: The core adjective special means belonging to one kind, so to specialise is to pull effort out of the general stream and sink it into one channel.
senses.whyCN: 核心名词 special 意为「属于某一类的」，因此 specialise 就是把精力从大流中抽出来，全部沉进一条窄渠。

senses.title: To work or practise in one narrow branch
senses.definition: to do one particular kind of work or trade as ones main occupation
senses.definitionCN: 把某一类工作或行业作为主要职业来做
senses.example: The firm specialises in small business accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司专门做小企业的账目。
senses.why: From choosing a field of study the word widens to choosing a field of paid work, and the narrow-channel image stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 从选择读书领域扩展到选择谋生的行当，窄渠的意象一点没变，只是水换成了生意。

senses.title: To become adapted to one function
senses.titleCN: （器官、细胞）特化；专门进化出某种功能
senses.definition: of a body part or cell, to develop a form that serves one particular function
senses.definitionCN: 指身体部位或细胞演化出服务于某一特定功能的形态
senses.example: These cells have specialised for sensing light.
senses.exampleCN: 这些细胞已经特化，专门用来感光。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the economic idea of the specialist and applied it to the body, so a cell that does one job well is said to specialise.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了经济学里「专才」的想法，把它用到身体上：一个细胞把一件差事做到极致，就叫特化。

senses.title: To make a product fit one use or place
senses.titleCN: 使专门化；为特定用途而改造
senses.definition: to modify a text, product, or service so that it suits one group, place, or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 修改文本、产品或服务，使其适合某一群体、地方或用途
senses.example: The teachers specialised the reading list for younger pupils.
senses.exampleCN: 老师们为低年级学生把这套书单做了专门化调整。
senses.why: From a person who chooses one niche, the verb turns to a thing that is trimmed to one niche, and the accent shifts from choosing to shaping.
senses.whyCN: 从「人选择小众领域」转到「物被裁剪到小众领域」，重心由选择变成了改造。

intro.en: Specialise is a nineteenth century English coinage built on special, from Latin specialis, and the suffix -ise that marks verbs of making or becoming.
intro.cn: specialise 是十九世纪英语用 special 加动词后缀 -ise 造出的词；special 来自拉丁语 specialis，-ise 表示「使……化」。

items.en: Species means a look or a kind, and specialis means belonging to one kind.
items.cn: species 意为外观或种类，specialis 意为「属于某一类的」。

items.en: Medieval Latin specialis appears in the phrase species specialissima, the narrowest kind in a logical classification.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 specialis 出现在术语 species specialissima 中，指逻辑分类里最窄的「种」。

items.en: English adopts special from Old French especial, meaning particular rather than general.
items.cn: 英语从古法语 especial 借入 special，意为特定的而非通用的。

items.en: Specialist first names a person devoted to one branch, and the noun speciality follows.
items.cn: specialist 先指专攻某一分支的人，名词 speciality 随后出现。

items.en: Specialise and specialize appear as verbs in the nineteenth century, first in scientific writing and soon in medicine and business.
items.cn: specialise 与 specialize 在十九世纪作为动词出现，最初见于科学写作，很快进入医学与商业。

items.en: The spelling divides: -ise is usual in British English, -ize in American English.
items.cn: 拼写分化为两派：英式常用 -ise，美式常用 -ize。

note.en: Specialise sits in a family built on Latin species, and it is close in meaning to concentrate and narrow down.
note.cn: specialise 属于拉丁语 species 一系的词族，含义上与 concentrate、narrow down 相邻。

entries.definition: a person who knows a great deal about one subject or field
a field one is expert in, or a particular product
a group of living things of the same kind
to give all attention or effort to one thing
to direct attention or effort towards one point
to spread across many cases rather than narrow to one
entries.definitionCN: 概括；泛化（与专门化相对）

normalIntro.en: Specialise means to turn the general into the special: one kind, one channel, one depth.
normalIntro.cn: specialise 就是把通用的变成专门的：一个种类、一条渠道、一个深度。

normal.en: The verb is built on special plus -ise, so to specialise is to make oneself special in one field.
normal.cn: 这个动词由 special 加 -ise 构成，所以 specialise 就是让自己在某一领域变得专门。

normal.en: Specialise takes in, so you specialise in surgery, not specialise surgery.
normal.cn: specialise 与 in 搭配，要说 specialize in surgery，而不能直接接宾语。

normal.en: The person is a specialist, the field is a speciality, and the act is specialisation.
normal.cn: 做的人是 specialist，那个领域是 speciality，这个行为是 specialisation。

normal.en: British spelling is -ise, American spelling is -ize; both are correct.
normal.cn: 英式拼写用 -ise，美式拼写用 -ize，两者都对。

normal.en: Compare generalise: generalise spreads out, specialise drills down.
normal.cn: 对比 generalise：generalise 向外铺开，specialise 向下钻深。

abstract.en: Picture a wide river suddenly funnelled into a narrow canal.
abstract.cn: 想象一条宽河突然被收进一条窄窄的运河。

abstract.en: Imagine a torch that gathers a wide glow into a single sharp beam.
abstract.cn: 想象一把把大片散光收成一束锐利光柱的手电筒。

abstract.en: Think of a body cell that gives up every other job to sense light.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细胞放下别的差事，只为感光而特化。

examples.en: This clinic specialises in children with hearing problems.
examples.cn: 这家诊所专门诊治有听力问题的儿童。

examples.en: She decided to specialise in translation after her first year.
examples.cn: 一年级结束后，她决定专攻翻译。

examples.en: The museum bought specialised equipment to protect old paper.
examples.cn: 博物馆购置了专门设备来保护旧纸张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「special + ize」——把注意力「塞」进一个特别的小格子里，只做那一件事；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 species（种类、外观）→ specialis（属于某一类的）→ 古法语 especial → 英语 special → 动词 specialise；-ise 表示「使……化」。

sensesIntro.en: From choosing one field of study, specialise widens to one kind of paid work, then to a body part or product shaped for a single job.
sensesIntro.cn: specialise 从选定一门学问出发，扩展到选定一种营生，再延伸到身体部位或产品为单一用途特化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller leaves the wide road for one narrow track.
core.cn: 核心意象：行人离开大道，拐进一条窄窄的小径。

branches.en: Studying one subject deeply comes straight from the narrow track.
branches.cn: 专攻一门学科，直接源自那条窄径的意象。

branches.en: Doing one kind of paid work is the trade side of the same choice.
branches.cn: 专门从事一种营生，是同一选择在职业上的对应。

branches.en: A cell shaped for one function is the biological descendant.
branches.cn: 为单一功能成形的细胞，是这一意象在生物学上的延伸。

branches.en: A product trimmed to one use is the object-side sense.
branches.cn: 为某一用途裁剪的产品，是这个词的物面义项。

branches.en: Both study and work senses share the move from many options to one.
branches.cn: 求学与谋生两个义项共享从多到一的收窄过程。

intro.en: Specialise is special plus the verb suffix -ise, and it heads a family with specialist, speciality, and specialisation.
intro.cn: specialise 由 special 加动词后缀 -ise 构成，并带出 specialist、speciality、specialisation 一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin species gives the whole family its idea of kind, and specialis narrows kind to one member.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 species 为整个词族提供「种类」的概念，specialis 则把种类收窄到某一种。

items.exampleCN: species 是整个词族的源头。

items.example: Specialis gives the English special.
items.exampleCN: specialis 给出英语的 special。

items.example: Special is the base of the verb.
items.exampleCN: special 是这个动词的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ise makes special into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 把 special 变成动词。

items.meaning: to make or become, American spelling
items.example: Specialize is the American form.
items.exampleCN: specialize 是美式写法。

items.meaning: a person who does or studies
items.example: The suffix -ist gives specialist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 specialist。

items.example: A specialist does one job well.
items.exampleCN: specialist 把一件事做得很好。

items.example: The suffix -ation gives specialisation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 specialisation。

items.example: The suffix -ity gives the noun speciality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成名词 speciality。

items.example: Speciality names the narrow field.
items.exampleCN: speciality 指那个专门的领域。

definition_zh: 专长；专业；专科；特色菜；特产
definition_en: a field of work or study that someone is expert in, or a product that a place or person is known for
core_image: 一条街上的小店门口挂着一块招牌，只写明一种拿手东西
scene: 海边小镇每家餐馆门口都写着本店的特色菜，游客循着这些菜名找上门来。Every restaurant in the seaside town posts its specialty outside, and tourists follow those names to the door.
sceneCN: 这里 specialty 是「特色菜、招牌货」（第 3 个义项：某地或某人以之出名的特别产品）；句意：海边小镇每家餐馆门口都写着本店的特色菜，游客循着这些菜名找上门来。

pos.zh: 专长；专业；专科；特色菜；特产

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根加 -ist 构成，义为「专家；专科医生」
同族动词（美式 specialize），义为「专攻；专门从事」
整个词族的基础词，义为「特别的；专门的」

senses.title: A particular field of study
senses.definition: the subject in which a student takes the larger part of their degree courses
senses.definitionCN: 学生在学位课程中投入最多的那一门学科
senses.example: Her specialty at university was marine biology.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学的主修专业是海洋生物学。
senses.why: The base special marks one kind out of many, and the noun turns that one kind into a chosen field of study.
senses.whyCN: 基础词 special 把「一类」从众多门类中挑出来，名词形式便把这个门类变成选定的一门学问。

senses.title: An area of professional expertise
senses.definition: the branch of work or knowledge in which a person is most skilled
senses.definitionCN: 某人在工作或知识中最擅长的那一分支
senses.example: Contract law is his specialty.
senses.exampleCN: 合同法是他的专长。
senses.why: The same narrow field is now attached to a person rather than a course, so the sense moves from study to skill.
senses.whyCN: 同一个窄领域，现在挂在一个人的本事上而不是课表上，义项便从「所学」滑到「所长」。

senses.title: A product a place or person is known for
senses.definition: a kind of food or goods that a particular place, shop, or maker is especially good at producing
senses.definitionCN: 某地、某店或某匠人特别擅长制作的食品或商品
senses.example: The bakery is famous for its specialty bread.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店以其特色面包出名。
senses.why: The expert field turns into an expert product: what a place does best becomes the thing it sells best, from cheese to cakes.
senses.whyCN: 「专长领域」转成「专长产品」：一个地方最会做什么，就成了它最拿得出手的东西，从奶酪到糕点都是如此。

senses.title: A specialist medical branch
senses.definition: a branch of medicine that deals with one group of organs or one kind of patient
senses.definitionCN: 专门处理某一类器官或某一类病人的医学分支
senses.example: The hospital has a specialty in heart failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院设有心衰专科。
senses.why: Medicine split into narrow branches in the nineteenth century, and each branch took the name specialty from the language of trade.
senses.whyCN: 医学在十九世纪分成众多狭窄分支，每个分支都借用商业里「专营」的说法，取名 specialty。

senses.title: A district known for one business
senses.definition: a part of a district or an industry set apart for one kind of trade or product
senses.definitionCN: 某一街区或行业中，集中做一种买卖或卖一种产品的部分
senses.example: The old town is still a specialty district for printing.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区至今仍是印务专门的地界。
senses.why: When many shops of one kind gather in one lane, the lane itself acquires a speciality, which is the place-side sense of the noun.
senses.whyCN: 同类店铺成片聚在一条街上，这条街本身也就有了「专营」，这是名词的地面义项。

intro.en: Specialty is a doublet of speciality: both come from Latin specialis, but specialty reached English by a shorter route through Old French.
intro.cn: specialty 与 speciality 是同源异形词，二者都出自拉丁语 specialis，但 specialty 经由古法语走了一条更短的路进入英语。

items.en: Species means a kind or appearance, and specialis means belonging to one kind.
items.cn: species 意为种类或外观，specialis 意为「属于某一类的」。

items.en: Specialis is used for the narrowest kind in logical classification.
items.cn: specialis 被用来指逻辑分类中最窄的「种」。

items.en: The Old French form especial gives English the noun spellings that end in -ty.
items.cn: 古法语形式 especial 为英语提供了以 -ty 结尾的名词拼写。

items.en: Specialty first appears in the fifteenth century; the Latin-derived rival speciality follows later.
items.cn: specialty 最早见于十五世纪；由拉丁语路径来的 英式形式 speciality 出现得更晚。

items.en: Trade and medicine give the noun its modern senses of a special product and a medical branch.
items.cn: 商业与医学赋予这个词现代含义：特色产品与医学专科。

items.en: American English prefers specialty, British English usually keeps speciality.
items.cn: 美式英语更常用 specialty，英式英语通常仍用 speciality。

note.en: Specialty shares the Latin species root with specialist and speciality, and is close in meaning to expertise and a local speciality.
note.cn: specialty 与 specialist、speciality 共享拉丁语 species 词根，含义上与 expertise、地方特产等说法相邻。

entries.definition: the British form of the same word
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的英式拼写形式

normalIntro.en: Specialty is the thing a person or place is special at, whether a subject, a skill, or a dish.
normalIntro.cn: specialty 就是一个人或一个地方「特别拿手」的东西，可以是一门学问、一种手艺，也可以是一道菜。

normal.en: Specialty is special plus a noun ending, so it names the one special thing.
normal.cn: specialty 由 special 加名词词尾构成，指的就是那件特别的东西。

normal.en: Keep the family together: specialize to study it, a specialist to practise it, a specialty to be good at it.
normal.cn: 把词族串起来：specialize 是去学它，specialist 是做它的人，specialty 是擅长的那一项。

normal.en: In a restaurant, the specialty of the house is the dish a chef is proud of.
normal.cn: 在餐馆里，the specialty of the house 就是厨师最得意的招牌菜。

normal.en: The plural does not double the g sound, it is specialties with -ies.
normal.cn: 复数不加第二个 i，而是把 y 变 i 加 es，写成 specialties。

normal.en: American English says specialty, British English usually says speciality.
normal.cn: 美式说 specialty，英式通常说 speciality。

abstract.en: Picture a shop window with a single dish on display.
abstract.cn: 想象一个橱窗里只摆着一道菜。

abstract.en: Imagine a doctor whose nameplate shows one hospital department.
abstract.cn: 想象一位医生门牌上只写着一个科室。

abstract.en: Think of a tourist holding a map marked with one local food in each town.
abstract.cn: 想象一位游客拿着地图，每个小镇上都只标着一种当地吃食。

examples.en: Translation has always been her specialty.
examples.cn: 翻译一直是她的专长。

examples.en: The town is known for its specialty cheeses.
examples.cn: 这个小镇以特色奶酪闻名。

examples.en: He trained in a medical specialty before returning to the village.
examples.cn: 他在一个医学专科受训后回到了村里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特殊+尔体」——一个地方只有它有形的「特色体」就是特产与专长；这只是谐音拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 species（种类）→ specialis（属于某一类的）→ 古法语路径 → 英语 special → specialty；与特别相关的名词后缀构成「专门的那一样」。

sensesIntro.en: Specialty starts as the one field a student picks, passes to a persons strongest branch, and then to the product or place that does that branch best.
sensesIntro.cn: specialty 先指学生选定的那一门学问，接着指一个人最擅长的分支，再转指把这一分支做到最好的产品与地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shop sign that names only one special thing.
core.cn: 核心意象：只写一样拿手东西的店铺招牌。

branches.en: A chosen field of study is the first narrow sense of the noun.
branches.cn: 学生选定的学科，是这个名词最早的窄义。

branches.en: A persons strongest branch moves the narrow field from course to skill.
branches.cn: 一个人最擅长的分支，把窄领域从课程挪到了本事上。

branches.en: A signature food or goods is the expert field turned into a product.
branches.cn: 招牌食品或特产，是专长领域变成了产品。

branches.en: A medical specialty is the same narrowing inside one profession.
branches.cn: 医学专科是同一套收窄逻辑在某一职业内部的表现。

branches.en: Both product and district senses point to one trade concentrated in one place.
branches.cn: 产品义项与街区义项都指向集中在同一处的一种营生。

intro.en: Specialty is special plus a noun ending, and it sits in a family with specialist, specialise, and speciality.
intro.cn: specialty 由 special 加名词词尾构成，与 specialist、specialise、speciality 同属一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin species gives the idea of kind, and specialis narrows it to one kind; the -ty ending marks a noun of quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 species 提供「种类」的概念，specialis 收窄到某一种，-ty 词尾则使这个词成为表性质的名词。

items.exampleCN: specialis 给出形容词 special。

definition_zh: 景象；奇观；壮观场面；演出；眼镜
definition_en: an impressive or unusual sight, a large public show, or the glasses worn to correct sight
core_image: 广场上人群齐齐抬头，看向一场令人屏息的大场面
scene: 节日当晚，城市广场上空烟花炸开，成千上万人仰头观看。On the festival night, fireworks burst above the city square and thousands of people looked up at the spectacle.
sceneCN: 这里 spectacle 是「壮观的场面、奇景」（第 1 个义项：引人注目的景象）；句意：节日当晚，城市广场上空烟花炸开，成千上万人仰头观看这场奇景。

pos.zh: 景象；奇观；壮观场面；演出；眼镜

derivatives.zh: spectacle 去掉词尾后加 -ar，义为「壮观的；惊人的」

spectacle 的复数，指「眼镜」

senses.title: An impressive public sight
senses.definition: a dramatic or impressive scene that attracts public attention
senses.definitionCN: 引人注目、令人惊叹的场面或景象
senses.example: The parade was a magnificent spectacle.
senses.exampleCN: 这场游行是一场壮观的景象。
senses.why: Latin spectare means to look at, so a spectacle is literally something worth looking at, a sight that pulls the eye.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 spectare 意为「观看」，所以 spectacle 字面就是「值得看的东西」，一种把目光吸过去的景象。

senses.title: A large public performance or show
senses.definition: an organised public show or display, often on a large scale
senses.definitionCN: 组织起来的、往往规模很大的公开演出或展示
senses.example: The opening ceremony was a spectacle of light and music.
senses.exampleCN: 开幕式是一场灯光与音乐的盛大演出。
senses.why: When the impressive sight is staged on purpose for an audience, the same word names the show itself.
senses.whyCN: 当那种令人惊叹的景象被有意搬到观众面前演出时，同一个词就转而指这场演出本身。

senses.title: A ridiculous or embarrassing scene
senses.titleCN: 出丑的场景；滑稽（或可悲）的景象
senses.definition: a scene that makes a person or group look foolish to onlookers
senses.definitionCN: 让某个人或一群人在旁人眼中显得愚蠢的场景
senses.example: He made a spectacle of himself at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上当众出了丑。
senses.why: Being looked at is not always pleasant, so the word tilts from admiration to mockery when the eyes of the crowd turn judgemental.
senses.whyCN: 被人看并不总是好事，当众人目光从赞叹变成审视，这个词就从「精彩」偏到了「可笑」。

senses.title: Glasses worn to correct sight
senses.definition: a pair of lenses in a frame, worn over the eyes to help a person see
senses.definitionCN: 装在镜框里、戴在眼上帮助视物的一对镜片
senses.example: The old teacher took off his spectacles to clean them.
senses.exampleCN: 老教师摘下眼镜来擦。
senses.why: The instrument that helps the eye look clearly was once called a spectacle in the singular, and the plural now names the pair.
senses.whyCN: 帮助眼睛看清东西的器具，早年单数就称 spectacle，后来用复数 spectacles 指这一副。

senses.title: A thing placed on view as an object of curiosity
senses.titleCN: 供人观看的展品；珍奇之物
senses.definition: an object put on display mainly because people want to look at it
senses.definitionCN: 主要因为人们想看一眼而摆出来展示的物件
senses.example: The museum keeps the old clock as a curious spectacle.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把这台旧钟当作珍奇展品保存着。
senses.why: The looking itself becomes the reason the object exists on display, which extends the sight sense from events to things shown.
senses.whyCN: 「看」本身成了这个物件被摆出来的理由，于是义项从事件延伸到被展出之物。

intro.en: Spectacle comes from Latin spectaculum, a show, from spectare, to look at, itself built on specere, to see.
intro.cn: spectacle 来自拉丁语 spectaculum（表演、景象），源于 spectare（观看），而 spectare 又出自 specere（看见）。

items.en: The root spek means to look at closely, and it also gives Latin spy words.
items.cn: 重构词根 spek 意为仔细观察，拉丁语中表示窥看的词也出自它。

items.en: Specere means to see, and spectare means to look at repeatedly.
items.cn: specere 意为看见，spectare 意为反复观看。

items.en: Spectaculum names a show or sight that entertains the crowd.
items.cn: spectaculum 指娱乐观众的表演或景象。

items.en: Old French spectacle brings the noun into English with its show sense intact.
items.cn: 古法语 spectacle 把这个名词带着「表演」之义带入英语。

items.en: The noun first marks a public sight or show, and by the fifteenth century it also means glasses.
items.cn: 这个词最早指公开的景象或演出，到十五世纪也用来指眼镜。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the grand sight and the everyday spectacles.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留「壮丽景象」与日常的「眼镜」两义。

note.en: Spectacle belongs to the Latin specere family of looking words and is close in meaning to sight, scene, and show.
note.cn: spectacle 属于拉丁语 specere「看」这一词族，含义上与 sight、scene、show 等词相邻。

entries.definition: extremely impressive to look at
a person who watches an event
a pair of glasses
something that is seen
what can be seen in one place
an elaborate public show or procession

normalIntro.en: Spectacle is a looking word: whatever makes the crowd turn its head is a spectacle.
normalIntro.cn: spectacle 是一个「看」的词：凡能让众人回头的，就是 spectacle。

normal.en: The root spec- means to look, as in spectator and inspect, so a spectacle is what is looked at.
normal.cn: 词根 spec- 意为「看」，spectator、inspect 都是如此，所以 spectacle 就是被看的东西。

normal.en: Make a spectacle of oneself means to draw unwanted eyes at a bad moment.
normal.cn: make a spectacle of oneself 就是在一个糟糕的时刻招来并不想要的目光。

normal.en: The plural spectacles also means glasses, because glasses help the eye look.
normal.cn: 复数 spectacles 同时表示「眼镜」，因为眼镜正是在帮眼睛看。

normal.en: Spectacular is the adjective, and it describes something that is wonderful to look at.
normal.cn: spectacular 是它的形容词，表示「看着非常精彩」。

normal.en: Compare spectator: the spectator watches, the spectacle is watched.
normal.cn: 对比 spectator：观众在看，景象是被看的。

abstract.en: Picture a whole crowd frozen with heads turned one way.
abstract.cn: 想象整片人群定住，头全朝同一个方向转过去。

abstract.en: Imagine a single pair of lenses held up in a hand against the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起一副镜片对着光。

abstract.en: Think of a man talking too loudly at a quiet party while everyone stares.
abstract.cn: 想象一场安静的聚会上，一个人说得太大声，所有人都在看他。

examples.en: The sunset over the sea was a breathtaking spectacle.
examples.cn: 海上的日落是令人屏息的美景。

examples.en: The trial turned into a public spectacle watched by thousands.
examples.cn: 这场审判变成了数千人围观的公开场面。

examples.en: Grandmother still wears her old spectacles for reading.
examples.cn: 外婆看报时还戴着她的老眼镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「思必看」——值得人「思」来「想」去、必「看」一眼的场面，就是奇观；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 specere（看见）→ spectare（观看）→ spectaculum（景象、表演）→ 古法语 spectacle → 英语 spectacle，核心义「被看见的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: From a sight worth looking at, spectacle moves to a staged show, then to a foolish scene, and finally to the thing that helps the eye look, the spectacles.
sensesIntro.cn: spectacle 从「值得一看的景象」出发，转为「被安排出来给人看的演出」，再转为「惹人侧目的出丑场面」，最后落到帮眼睛去看的物件，即眼镜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd looking up at one amazing sight.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群一起抬头看向一个惊人的景象。

branches.en: An impressive public sight is the plain sense of something looked at.
branches.cn: 壮观的公开景象，就是「被看之物」的本义。

branches.en: A staged show is the impressive sight made on purpose.
branches.cn: 盛大演出，就是把惊人景象刻意制造出来。

branches.en: An embarrassing scene comes when the crowd stops admiring and starts judging.
branches.cn: 出丑场面出现于人群从赞叹转为评判之时。

branches.en: Glasses are the instrument that helps the eye do the looking.
branches.cn: 眼镜是帮助眼睛去看的器具。

branches.en: Both a show and a curious object exist to be looked at.
branches.cn: 演出与珍奇展品，都是为了让人看而存在。

intro.en: Spectacle is built on the Latin root spect- for looking, the same root behind spectator, inspect, and spectacular.
intro.cn: spectacle 建立在表示「看」的拉丁词根 spect- 上，spectator、inspect、spectacular 都同出此根。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere means to see, spectare means to look at, and the suffix -culum forms a noun of means or result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere 意为看见，spectare 意为观看，后缀 -culum 构成表示工具或结果的名词。

items.example: Specere is the deepest layer of the word.
items.exampleCN: specere 是这个词最深的层次。

items.example: Spectare brings the idea of watching.
items.exampleCN: spectare 带来注视的含义。

items.example: The suffix -culum makes spectaculum.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -culum 构成 spectaculum。

items.example: The root spect- runs through many English words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 spect- 贯穿许多英语词。

items.example: The suffix -ar gives spectacular.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ar 构成 spectacular。

items.example: The suffix -or gives spectator.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 spectator。

items.example: A spectator watches a spectacle.
items.exampleCN: 观众观看景象。

items.example: The prefix in- makes inspect, to look into.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 inspect，表示往里看。

items.example: Inspect shows the same looking root.
items.exampleCN: inspect 展示同一个「看」的词根。

definition_zh: 观众；看台观众；旁观者
definition_en: a person who watches an event, especially a sports event, without taking part in it
core_image: 看台上伸长脖子的人群，眼睛一齐望向场地中央
scene: 球场四周的看台上挤满了人，他们只为看球而来。By half time, the spectators were on their feet, shouting for the home team.
sceneCN: 这里 spectator 是「看台观众」（第 2 个义项：坐在看台座位上观看比赛的人）；句意：到了半场，看台上的观众纷纷站起来，为主队呐喊。

derivatives.zh: 由动词后缀 -ate 回构而成，义为「观看；当观众」
加后缀 -ial 构成，义为「观众的；旁观性质的」
加后缀 -ship 表示身份或状态，义为「观众身份；观看行为」

senses.title: A person watching an event
senses.definition: someone who watches an event, a game, or a show without taking part in it
senses.definitionCN: 不参与其中、只在旁观看某项活动、比赛或演出的人
senses.example: Over twenty thousand spectators filled the stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 两万多名观众挤满了体育场。
senses.why: The Latin verb spectare means to look at and keep looking, so a spectator is literally one who keeps watching.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 spectare 意为「注视、持续地看」，所以 spectator 字面就是不断看的人。

senses.title: A member of a seated crowd
senses.definition: a member of the crowd who watches from seats, especially at a sports ground or arena
senses.definitionCN: 坐在座位上观看比赛的人群中的一员，尤指在体育场或球馆里
senses.example: The steel stands now hold thousands of spectators every weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 如今每逢周末，这座钢制看台能容纳数千名观众。
senses.why: Modern sport turned watching into a shared paid experience, so spectator came to name a person in a seated crowd.
senses.whyCN: 现代体育把观看变成了付费的集体体验，spectator 因此也被用来指看台上成群的观众。

senses.title: Someone who watches without acting
senses.definition: a person who watches a situation without becoming involved in it
senses.definitionCN: 只观察某个局面而不介入其中的人
senses.example: We could not stay spectators while the town was in danger.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇处于危险之中，我们不能只做旁观者。
senses.why: The image of watching from a distance easily becomes a criticism, because a spectator does nothing about what is happening.
senses.whyCN: 「站在远处看」的画面很容易带上批评意味，因为旁观者对眼前发生的事什么也不做。

senses.title: An observer of everyday life
senses.definition: a person who observes human behaviour calmly, as writers and visitors sometimes do
senses.definitionCN: 平静地观察人们行为的人，作家或外来访客常这样做
senses.example: The novel describes the war through the eyes of a young spectator.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说通过一个年轻旁观者的眼睛来描写战争。
senses.why: A writer or traveller watches life the way a spectator watches a game, so the word also names a calm observer.
senses.whyCN: 作家或旅行者看生活，就像观众看比赛一样，因此这个词也指平静的观察者。

senses.title: Spectator shoes
senses.definition: a two-coloured formal shoe with a decorative band across the toe, also called a spectator shoe
senses.definitionCN: 鞋头横着一条对比色带的双色正式皮鞋，也称观赏鞋
senses.example: He wore brown and white spectators to the summer gathering.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着棕白双色皮鞋去参加夏日聚会。
senses.why: The shoe was made to be looked at rather than worked in, so it borrowed the name of the watching crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这种鞋是给人看的，不是穿来干活的，于是借用了「观看」这一名字。

senses.title: The spectator stance
senses.definition: a detached position of watching in which someone judges actions but takes no part
senses.definitionCN: 只评价而不参与的疏离位置，看着别人行动而自己不介入
senses.example: A critic should not write from the spectator stance alone.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家不应只站在旁观者的位置上写作。
senses.why: The idea of watching from outside grows into a stance, a way of standing apart from events.
senses.whyCN: 从外面观看的观念进一步引申出一种姿态，即与事件保持距离地站着。

intro.en: Spectator comes from Latin spectator, a watcher, from the verb spectare, to look at, a frequentative of specere, to see.
intro.cn: spectator 来自拉丁语 spectator（观看者），源于动词 spectare（注视），而 spectare 是 specere（看见）的反复动词形式。

items.en: Specere means to look at or see.
items.cn: specere 意为看、望见。

items.en: Spectare, a frequentative of specere, means to keep looking at.
items.cn: spectare 是 specere 的反复动词形式，意为持续注视。

items.en: Spectator names a person who watches.
items.cn: spectator 指观看的人。

items.en: French spectateur brings the Latin form into wider European use.
items.cn: 法语 spectateur 把这一拉丁词形带入更广的欧洲语言使用中。

items.en: First recorded in English in the sixteenth century, naming those who watch a play or a game.
items.cn: 十六世纪首次见于英语，指观看戏剧或比赛的人。

items.en: Modern English extends it to seesaws and grows a verb, spectate.
items.cn: 现代英语把它拓展到体育观众，并回构出动词 spectate。

note.en: Spectator belongs to the Latin family of looking: specere, spectare, aspect, inspect, and the everyday audience.
note.cn: spectator 属于拉丁语「看」这一词族：specere、spectare、aspect、inspect，以及日常用的 audience。

entries.definition: an impressive public show
very impressive to look at
to look at something closely in order to check it
the people who watch or listen to a play or performance
a person who watches something happen without joining in
a person who watches a particular thing

normalIntro.en: Spectator is built on the Latin root spec-, to look, so the word is a person who is there only to look.
normalIntro.cn: spectator 建立在拉丁词根 spec-（看）之上，所以这个词指的是只为看而来的人。

normal.en: Spect- appears in spectacle, spectacular, and inspect, all about looking.
normal.cn: 词根 spect- 出现在 spectacle、spectacular 与 inspect 中，都与「看」有关。

normal.en: A spectator sport is a game played mainly to be watched.
normal.cn: spectator sport 指主要为供人观看而举行的比赛。

normal.en: A mere spectator is someone who only stands by and watches.
normal.cn: a mere spectator 就是指只在旁边看着的人。

normal.en: Compare actor and spectator: one takes part, the other only watches.
normal.cn: 对比 actor 与 spectator：一个参与其中，一个只是观看。

normal.en: The verb spectate was formed back from the noun, as in they came to spectate.
normal.cn: 动词 spectate 是由名词回构而成，如他们来观赛。

abstract.en: Picture a long line of eyes all turned toward the same point.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排眼睛一齐转向同一个点。

abstract.en: Imagine sitting in a cold seat with a fresh ticket in hand.
abstract.cn: 想象手里攥着刚买的票，坐在冰凉的座位上。

abstract.en: Think of someone behind a window who never opens the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在窗后，却始终不去开门。

examples.en: The race drew spectators from across the country.
examples.cn: 这场比赛吸引了全国各地的观众。

examples.en: She insisted on being more than a passive spectator in the debate.
examples.cn: 她坚持不做辩论中被动观看的旁观者。

examples.en: Thousands of spectators waited outside the stadium for hours.
examples.cn: 成千上万的观众在体育场外等了好几个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯佩克特」读起来像「死盯客」——死死盯着场上的那个人，就是观众；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 specere（看见）→ spectare（注视，反复形式）→ 拉丁语 spectator（观看者）→ 法语 spectateur → 英语 spectator，核心义「持续地看的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Spectator begins with a person who watches a game, then widens to a seated crowd, a passive bystander, a calm observer, and finally a figurative stance.
sensesIntro.cn: spectator 从观看比赛的人出发，逐渐扩展到看台上的观众、袖手旁观者、平静的观察者，最后引申为一种观众的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a packed stand of faces turned toward the field.
core.cn: 核心意象：看台上挤满面孔，全都朝向场地。

branches.en: The basic sense is a person who watches an event.
branches.cn: 基本义项是观看活动的人。

branches.en: Sport and ticketed seating produce the crowd sense.
branches.cn: 体育和售票座位产生了「看台上的观众」这一义项。

branches.en: Watching without acting gives the reproachful bystander sense.
branches.cn: 只看不动手，带出了带批评意味的旁观者义项。

branches.en: A writer observing life is a calm spectator of events.
branches.cn: 观察生活的作家就是事件的平静旁观者。

branches.en: The stance of watching and the shoe made to be admired both keep the idea of looking on.
branches.cn: 观看的姿态和供人欣赏的双色皮鞋，都保留了「在旁观看」的理念。

intro.en: Spectator is built on the Latin root spec-, with spectare, -ator, and a set of English relatives such as inspect and spectacle.
intro.cn: spectator 建立在拉丁词根 spec- 之上，涉及 spectare、后缀 -ator，以及 inspect、spectacle 等一批英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere means to see, spectare means to keep looking, and -ator marks the person who does it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere 意为看见，spectare 意为持续注视，后缀 -ator 表示做这件事的人。

items.example: The root spec- is the seed of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 spec- 是整个词族的种子。

items.meaning: to watch, to keep looking at
items.example: Spectare adds the idea of a longer look.
items.exampleCN: spectare 增加了「看得更久」的含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ator turns a verb into a person.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ator 把动作变成做动作的人。

items.example: Fans came to spectate the final.
items.exampleCN: 球迷们来观看决赛。

items.example: The parade was a splendid spectacle.
items.exampleCN: 游行是一场壮观的景象。

items.example: The view from the tower was spectacular.
items.exampleCN: 从塔上看到的景色非常壮观。

items.example: Officials inspect the equipment each season.
items.exampleCN: 官员每季检查设备。

items.meaning: one way of looking at something
items.example: Aspect keeps the idea of a look from a direction.
items.exampleCN: aspect 保留了「从某个方向看」的意思。

items.meaning: state of being such a person
items.meaningCN: 表示此类身份的词尾组合
items.example: The noun spectatorship names the role of watching.
items.exampleCN: 名词 spectatorship 指观众这一身份。

definition_zh: 菠菜；菠菜叶；菠菜做的菜
definition_en: a vegetable with large dark green leaves that is eaten cooked or in salad
core_image: 一捆带着红根的深绿色叶子，叶片皱起，叶柄鲜绿
scene: 菜市场里，摊主把深绿色的叶子捆成一把，根上还带着红泥。The cook washed the spinach, then dropped it into a pot of boiling water.
sceneCN: 这里 spinach 是「菠菜」（第 1 个义项：可作为蔬菜食用的深绿色叶菜）；句意：厨师把菠菜洗净，然后丢进一锅沸水里。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -y 构成的口语形容词，义为「带菠菜味的」
复合构词，义为「像菠菜的」，多用于描述叶类植物
复合形容词，义为「菠菜绿的」，形容深绿色

senses.title: The green-leafed vegetable
senses.definition: a plant with large dark green leaves that is grown as a vegetable
senses.definitionCN: 一种叶片宽大、深绿色、作为蔬菜栽培的植物
senses.example: Spinach grows quickly in cool weather.
senses.exampleCN: 菠菜在凉爽的天气里长得很快。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply the plant itself, the leafy thing that comes up out of the ground.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项就是这种植物本身，即从土里长出来的叶菜。

senses.title: The leaves used as food
senses.definition: the leaves of this plant eaten as food, either raw or cooked
senses.definitionCN: 这种植物的叶子，生吃或煮熟后作为食物
senses.example: Add a handful of spinach at the end of cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 烹饪快结束时加一把菠菜。
senses.why: The part we eat is the leaf, so the same word easily moves from the plant to the food on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 我们吃的是叶子，所以同一个词很自然从植物转到盘子里的食物。

senses.title: A dish made from spinach
senses.definition: a dish or side course prepared mainly from spinach, such as creamed spinach
senses.definitionCN: 以菠菜为主要原料做成的菜肴或配菜，如奶油菠菜
senses.example: The restaurant serves spinach with pine nuts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家餐馆供应松子菠菜。
senses.why: In menus and kitchens the vegetable name stands for the finished dish, the way rice or soup names a course.
senses.whyCN: 在菜单和厨房里，蔬菜的名字常代表成品菜，就像米饭或汤代表一道菜一样。

senses.title: The plant in agriculture
senses.definition: the crop planted and harvested on farms for market
senses.definitionCN: 在农田里为供应市场而种植和收获的作物
senses.example: Farmers here harvest spinach twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农户一年收获两次菠菜。
senses.why: Once a plant is grown as a crop, its name also names the harvest, the acre, and the trade.
senses.whyCN: 一种植物成为作物之后，它的名字也指收成、田亩和这门生意。

senses.title: A colour like spinach
senses.definition: a deep dull green colour said to be like the colour of spinach leaves
senses.definitionCN: 一种深而暗的绿色，被形容为像菠菜叶的颜色
senses.example: The walls were painted a dull spinach green.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁刷成了一种暗沉的菠菜绿。
senses.why: Food words often become colour words, because the strongest thing about spinach is its deep green.
senses.whyCN: 食物词常变成颜色词，因为菠菜最强烈的印象就是那种深绿。

intro.en: Spinach reached English through Old French espinache, from Medieval Latin spinachium, which probably traces back through Arabic to Persian aspand or isfand.
intro.cn: spinach 经由古法语 espinache 进入英语，上溯到中世纪拉丁语 spinachium，一般认为再经阿拉伯语追溯到波斯语 aspand 或 isfand。

items.en: Persian isfand or aspand names the plant; the exact Old Persian form is uncertain.
items.cn: 波斯语 isfand 或 aspand 指这种植物；更早的古波斯语形式来源不确定。

items.en: Arabic isfanakh carries the plant name westward as spinach spread through the Islamic world.
items.cn: 随着菠菜在伊斯兰世界传播，阿拉伯语 isfanakh 把这一植物名带向西方。

items.en: Medieval Latin spinachium records the plant in European texts.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 spinachium 在欧洲文献中记录了这一植物。

items.en: Old French espinache takes the word from Latin and drops the heaviest cluster of consonants.
items.cn: 古法语 espinache 从拉丁语借用，并简化了沉重的辅音群。

items.en: English spinache appears in the fourteenth century, later respelled as spinach.
items.cn: 英语 spinache 于十四世纪出现，后来拼写逐渐演变为 spinach。

items.en: Modern English keeps the spelling spinach and adds its colour and dish uses.
items.cn: 现代英语沿用 spinach 的拼写，并增添了颜色和菜肴的用法。

note.en: Spinach is a borrowed plant name with no native English root; its relatives are other leafy greens and other borrowed vegetable words.
note.cn: spinach 是借来的植物名，没有英语本土词根；它的近亲是其他叶菜和别的借入蔬菜词。

entries.definition: to turn round quickly
entries.definitionCN: 旋转（只是与 spinach 开头几个字母相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to let liquid fall out of a container
entries.definitionCN: 洒出；溢出（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a small early keyboard instrument
entries.definitionCN: 斯皮内特琴（小型的早期键盘乐器，只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a leafy vegetable eaten raw in salad
a dark green leafy vegetable of the cabbage family
a round vegetable with thick green leaves

normalIntro.en: Spinach is a borrowed vegetable name with a Persian and Arabic past, so remember it as a dictionary visitor rather than a native root.
normalIntro.cn: spinach 是一个借入的蔬菜名，源头在波斯语和阿拉伯语，所以要把它当作外来词来记，而不是英语本土词根。

normal.en: The -ach ending is rare in English, like the -ach of stomach.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ach 在英语中很少见，和 stomach 的结尾相似。

normal.en: Spinach pairs with leafy: spinach is a leafy green.
normal.cn: spinach 常与 leafy 搭配：菠菜是一种叶菜。

normal.en: The common phrase is a bunch of spinach, a whole bundle for cooking.
normal.cn: 常用说法 a bunch of spinach，指一整把用来做菜的菠菜。

normal.en: Spinach is a borrowed plant name, unlike native lettuce, so its spelling has ch.
normal.cn: spinach 是借来的植物名，与本土词 lettuce 不同，所以拼写里带 ch。

normal.en: Creamed spinach, spinach salad, and spinach soup show the three common food uses.
normal.cn: 奶油菠菜、菠菜沙拉和菠菜汤展示了三种常见的食用方式。

abstract.en: Picture a deep green plant standing up in the garden row.
abstract.cn: 想象一株深绿色的植物在菜畦里立着。

abstract.en: Imagine a bunch of wet leaves dripping onto the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一大把湿叶子在台面上滴水。

abstract.en: Think of a pink root tied with a string, waiting to be eaten.
abstract.cn: 想象一根带红的根被绳子捆着，等着被吃掉。

examples.en: She added spinach to the soup just before serving.
examples.cn: 上汤之前她往汤里加了菠菜。

examples.en: Doctors suggest that children eat leafy greens such as spinach.
examples.cn: 医生建议孩子吃菠菜这类叶菜。

examples.en: The spinach in this garden looks ready to pick.
examples.cn: 园子里的菠菜看起来可以采收了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯皮尼奇」听起来像「撕皮泥吃」——把菜叶的皮撕开、洗去泥，就能下锅吃了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 波斯语 aspand／isfand（菠菜）→ 阿拉伯语 isfanakh → 中世纪拉丁语 spinachium → 古法语 espinache → 英语 spinach，核心义「深绿色叶菜」。

sensesIntro.en: Spinach starts as the plant, passes to its edible leaves, then to dishes, crops, and at last a colour.
sensesIntro.cn: spinach 先指这种植物，再指可食用的叶子，然后是菜肴、作物，最后成为一种颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bunch of dark green leaves with red-tinged stems.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把深绿色叶子，叶柄根部泛红。

branches.en: The plant itself is the literal starting point.
branches.cn: 植物本身是字面意义的起点。

branches.en: The edible leaves take the name onto the plate.
branches.cn: 可食用的叶子把词带到了餐盘上。

branches.en: Dishes and crops extend the name into kitchens and markets.
branches.cn: 菜肴和作物把词扩展到厨房与市场。

branches.en: The strong colour gives the word a paint-like sense.
branches.cn: 强烈的颜色给这个词带来类似颜料名称的义项。

branches.en: Both the leaf and its green share one source in the plant.
branches.cn: 叶子和它的绿色都来自同一株植物。

intro.en: Spinach is not built from English affixes; its structure is a borrowed whole word from Persian and Arabic through Latin and French.
intro.cn: spinach 并不是由英语词缀拼成的；它的结构是一整个借词，从波斯语、阿拉伯语经拉丁语和法语传入。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form spinachium and the Old French espinache carry the borrowed stem; the word has no productive Latin affix of its own.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词形 spinachium 与古法语 espinache 承载了借入的词干；这个词本身没有能产的拉丁词缀。

items.example: Isfanakh is the Arabic link in the chain.
items.exampleCN: isfanakh 是词源链中的阿拉伯语环节。

items.example: Spinachium appears in later Latin writing.
items.exampleCN: spinachium 见于后期的拉丁文文献。

items.meaningCN: 植物名词尾，并非真正的后缀
items.example: The ending -ach is carried over, not added.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ach 是原样带来的，不是后加的。

items.example: Spinach keeps the borrowed shape.
items.exampleCN: spinach 保留了借入时的词形。

items.example: The suffix -y forms the informal spinachy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成口语的 spinachy。

items.example: Spinachy is used in casual speech.
items.exampleCN: spinachy 多用于口语。

items.example: The suffix -like forms spinach-like.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 spinach-like。

items.example: Spinach is the most common leafy green in the fridge.
items.exampleCN: 菠菜是冰箱里最常见的叶菜。

items.example: Greens like spinach are rich in iron.
items.exampleCN: 菠菜这类叶菜含铁丰富。

definition_zh: 螺旋；螺旋形；盘旋；螺旋式上升或下降；螺旋式的
definition_en: a curve that winds continuously around a central point while moving steadily upward or outward, or a process that changes in such a pattern
core_image: 一圈一圈由内向外铺开的线，像蜗牛壳上的旋纹
scene: 楼梯绕着中轴向上盘了几圈，越走越高。A narrow stair winds in a tight spiral up to the bell tower.
sceneCN: 这里 spiral 是「螺旋形」（第 1 个义项：绕中心一圈圈上升或外扩的曲线）；句意：一道窄楼梯呈紧凑的螺旋状向上通往钟楼。

pos.zh: 螺旋；螺旋形；螺旋式上升或下降
盘旋；螺旋式上升或下降；急剧起伏

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「呈螺旋状地」
加动词后缀 -ize，义为「把食物切成螺旋丝」
现在分词名词化，义为「盘旋；螺旋式变化的过程」

senses.title: A winding curve
senses.definition: a shape made by a line that winds continuously around a central point while moving steadily upward or outward
senses.definitionCN: 一条绕中心连续旋转、同时不断上升或外扩所形成的形状
senses.example: The shell of a snail forms a perfect spiral.
senses.exampleCN: 蜗牛的壳构成了一个完美的螺旋。
senses.why: The Latin spiralis comes from spira, a coil, so the word begins as the shape itself, a line that keeps turning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 spiralis 来自 spira（线圈），因此这个词首先指形状本身，即一条不断弯转的线。

senses.title: A winding path or structure
senses.definition: something built or laid out in the shape of a spiral, such as a staircase or a road
senses.definitionCN: 按螺旋形建造或铺设的物体，如楼梯或道路
senses.example: They climbed the spiral of stone steps to the tower.
senses.exampleCN: 他们沿着盘旋的石阶登上塔楼。
senses.why: Once the shape is named, buildings and paths made in that shape take the name directly.
senses.whyCN: 形状一旦有了名字，按该形状建造的建筑和道路就直接沿用这个名字。

senses.title: A process of steady worsening
senses.definition: a process in which one problem causes another and the situation gets steadily worse or better
senses.definitionCN: 一个问题引发另一个问题、局势不断恶化或好转的过程
senses.example: Job losses began an economic spiral.
senses.exampleCN: 失业开始引发一轮经济螺旋式下滑。
senses.why: The figure moving away from the centre in widening rings pictures a situation that grows worse with each turn.
senses.whyCN: 图形一圈比一圈远离中心，正好形象地表现局势每转一圈就更糟。

senses.title: To wind or move in a spiral
senses.definition: to move or develop in a spiral, curving round while rising or falling
senses.definitionCN: 以螺旋方式运动或发展，边旋转边上升或下降
senses.example: Prices spiralled after the bad harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 歉收之后物价一路飞涨。
senses.why: The noun became a verb, so the shape turns into a movement that the subject performs.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成了动词，形状于是变成主语所进行的运动。

senses.title: A rise that never stops
senses.definition: to rise or grow quickly and steadily, often beyond what people expect
senses.definitionCN: 迅速而持续地上升或增长，常超出人们的预期
senses.example: Costs spiralled out of control within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 成本在一个月内螺旋式失控。
senses.why: An upward spiral has no natural stopping point, so the verb often names a rise that keeps feeding on itself.
senses.whyCN: 向上的螺旋没有天然的停止点，所以这个动词常指一种自我加码的上升。

senses.title: Shaped like a spiral
senses.definition: winding round in a spiral, used before a noun to describe shape or pattern
senses.definitionCN: 呈螺旋状弯曲的，置于名词前描述形状或图案
senses.example: A spiral notebook lies open on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 一本线圈笔记本摊开在书桌上。
senses.why: English nouns freely work as adjectives, so the shape word also describes the shape of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 英语名词可以便利地转作形容词，因此表示形状的词也能直接描述某物。

intro.en: Spiral comes from Latin spiralis, of spirals, from spira, a coil or a twisted thing, which goes back to Greek speira, a winding or a coil.
intro.cn: spiral 来自拉丁语 spiralis（螺旋状的），源于 spira（线圈、缠绕之物），更早可追溯到希腊语 speira（缠绕、线圈）。

items.en: Greek speira means a coil or a twisted thing.
items.cn: 希腊语 speira 意为线圈、缠绕之物。

items.en: Latin spira takes over the coil, and spira also names the base of a winding column.
items.cn: 拉丁语 spira 继承了「线圈」之义，同时也指螺旋柱的柱础。

items.en: Spiralis means of a spiral or winding shape.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 spiralis 意为呈螺旋状的。

items.en: French spirale carries the adjective into scientific and architectural writing.
items.cn: 法语 spirale 把这个形容词带入科学与建筑写作。

items.en: English spiral first names the winding shape, then its structures.
items.cn: 英语 spiral 先指盘旋的形状，再指呈此形状的物体。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb use and the figurative spiral of worsening.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了动词用法以及「螺旋式恶化」的比喻义。

note.en: Spiral belongs to the Latin family of coils (spira), and sits near coil, helix, and the looser swirl.
note.cn: spiral 属于拉丁语「线圈」（spira）词族，与 coil、helix 以及较宽泛的 swirl 相邻。

entries.definition: the tall pointed top of a church tower
entries.definitionCN: 教堂塔楼尖顶（与 spira 同源，古人把螺旋柱础叫作 spire）

entries.definition: the non-physical part of a person
entries.definitionCN: 精神；灵魂（与 spira 同源，原义与呼吸有关）

entries.definition: spiral, in Spanish
entries.definitionCN: 西班牙语的「螺旋」，与英语同源于拉丁语 spira

a curve that winds around a central axis like a spring
a twisting movement or shape

normalIntro.en: Spiral is built on the Latin coil spira, so think of a line that keeps turning while it moves.
normalIntro.cn: spiral 建立在拉丁语「线圈」spira 之上，所以要把它想成一条边转边走的线。

normal.en: Compare spire and spirit, both from spira, and all three carry the twist.
normal.cn: 对比 spire 与 spirit，三者都来自 spira，都带有「缠绕」的意思。

normal.en: A spiral staircase and a spiral notebook show the shape in buildings and paper.
normal.cn: 螺旋楼梯和线圈笔记本分别在建筑和纸品上体现了这种形状。

normal.en: A downward spiral describes a situation that gets worse with each turn.
normal.cn: a downward spiral 形容一圈比一圈更糟的处境。

normal.en: British English writes spiralling, American English writes spiraling.
normal.cn: 英式英语写作 spiralling，美式英语写作 spiraling。

normal.en: Spiral often pairs with out of control, as in costs spiralled out of control.
normal.cn: spiral 常与 out of control 搭配，如成本螺旋式失控。

abstract.en: Picture a snail shell against a pale sky.
abstract.cn: 想象淡色天空下的蜗牛壳。

abstract.en: Imagine climbing stairs that turn round and round the same post.
abstract.cn: 想象爬一道绕着同一根柱子一圈圈转的楼梯。

abstract.en: Think of water going down a drain in ever smaller rings.
abstract.cn: 想象水顺着下水道一圈圈变小地流下去。

examples.en: The road spirals up the mountain in gentle curves.
examples.cn: 道路以平缓的弧线盘旋着上山。

examples.en: Rumours of a new tax sent prices into a spiral.
examples.cn: 新税传闻让物价陷入螺旋式上涨。

examples.en: She drew a spiral on the corner of the page.
examples.cn: 她在页角画了一个螺旋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯派若」听起来像「趴着一圈绕」——一圈接一圈地绕着走，就是螺旋；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 speira（缠绕、线圈）→ 拉丁语 spira（线圈、螺旋柱础）→ 中世纪拉丁语 spiralis（螺旋状的）→ 法语 spirale → 英语 spiral，核心义「绕着中心一圈圈转」。

sensesIntro.en: Spiral travels from a shape, to things built in that shape, to worsening processes, to the verbs of winding and rising, and finally to an adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: spiral 从一种形状，走到按该形状建造的物体，再引申为恶化的过程、盘旋与攀升的动词，最后成为形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that turns round and round while it climbs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条边转边往上升的线。

branches.en: The winding curve is the original sense.
branches.cn: 盘旋的曲线是最初的义项。

branches.en: The noun and the adjective describe structures built in this shape.
branches.cn: 名词和形容词都描述按这种形状建造的结构。

branches.en: The widening rings become a picture of steady worsening.
branches.cn: 越转越大的圈变成对持续恶化的描绘。

branches.en: The verb takes over the movement of the curve.
branches.cn: 动词承接了曲线的运动方式。

branches.en: An upward spiral has no stop, so it names a runaway rise.
branches.cn: 向上的螺旋没有终点，因此指失控的攀升。

intro.en: Spiral is built on the Greek and Latin coil spira, with the adjective ending -al and English relatives such as spire and spirit.
intro.cn: spiral 建立在希腊语与拉丁语的「线圈」spira 之上，既带形容词词尾 -al，又与 spire、spirit 等英语词同族。

latinIntro.en: Greek speira and Latin spira mean coil, and the Latin ending -alis forms spiralis, of a coil.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 speira 与拉丁语 spira 意为线圈，拉丁语词尾 -alis 构成 spiralis，义为「线圈的」。

items.example: Spira is the stem the whole family shares.

items.meaningCN: 表示与某物相关的词尾
items.example: The suffix -al gives English spiral its adjective form.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 给英语 spiral 带来形容词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms spirally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 spirally。

items.example: The suffix -ise forms the British spelling of spiralise.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 构成英式拼写 spiralise。

items.example: Spire kept the old coil shape in its meaning.
items.exampleCN: spire 保留了旧词中线圈形状的意思。

items.example: Spirit shares the spiral stem through Latin spiritus.
items.exampleCN: spirit 经由拉丁语 spiritus 共享这一词干。

items.meaning: to cut food into long curls

senses.title: Drops of liquid thrown into the air
senses.definition: a mass of small drops of liquid thrown into the air by a moving object or person
senses.definitionCN: 物体或人运动时把液体激起、四散飞溅的小水珠团
senses.example: The stone hit the lake with a loud splash.
senses.exampleCN: 石头砸进湖里，溅起一大片水花，发出响声。
senses.why: The word first names the spray itself, the visible result of liquid being struck hard.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最先命名的是飞溅本身，也就是液体受到猛烈撞击后看得见的结果。

senses.title: To cause a liquid to fly up
senses.definition: to make a liquid fly through the air and land on something, often deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 使液体飞起并落到某物上，常带有主动泼的动作
senses.example: She splashed cold water on her face to wake up.
senses.exampleCN: 她往脸上泼冷水让自己清醒。
senses.why: Once the spray has a name, the verb grows from it naming the act of throwing water that way.
senses.whyCN: 水花有了名称之后，动词随之长出来，用来说把水那样甩出去的动作。

senses.title: To walk through water noisily
senses.definition: to move through water or mud so that liquid is thrown about, often for fun
senses.definitionCN: 在水或泥里走动，把水趟得四处飞溅，常带玩闹意味
senses.example: The children splashed through the puddles on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在回家路上一路踩着水坑啪啦啪啦地走。
senses.why: Walking through shallow water produces repeated small sprays, so the noun extends to the noisy walking action.
senses.whyCN: 在浅水里走路会不断激起小水花，所以名词延伸为这种带响声的行走。

senses.title: The sound of liquid being struck
senses.definition: the noise made when a liquid is hit or when something falls into it
senses.definitionCN: 液体被击打或有东西掉进液体时发出的声音
senses.example: We heard a splash and then laughter from the pool.
senses.exampleCN: 我们听见扑通一声，随后泳池那边传来笑声。
senses.why: The spray and the noise happen together, so the same word names the sound the eye and ear receive at once.
senses.whyCN: 水花和声音同时出现，于是同一个词也用来命名眼睛和耳朵同时接收到的那种声音。

senses.title: A bright patch of colour
senses.definition: a small area of bright colour that stands out against its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 在一片背景中格外醒目的一小块鲜艳颜色
senses.example: A splash of red curtain brightened the plain room.
senses.exampleCN: 一抹鲜红的窗帘让朴素的房间亮了起来。
senses.why: Colour thrown onto a dull surface looks like paint thrown onto water, so the visual spray sense extends to design.
senses.whyCN: 把颜色甩在暗淡表面上，看上去就像颜料甩进水里，于是视觉上的飞溅义延伸到设计领域。

senses.title: A small amount added to a drink
senses.definition: a small quantity of a liquid added to a drink or dish to give flavour
senses.definitionCN: 为调味而往饮料或菜里加的一点点液体
senses.example: He added a splash of milk to his coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 他往咖啡里加了一点牛奶。
senses.why: Pouring a little liquid makes one audible splash, and that single unit of sound became the unit of measure.
senses.whyCN: 倒一点点液体只会响一声，这一声音量单位就被借用成了计量的单位。

senses.title: To spread large pictures in a layout
senses.definition: to print a story or photograph across a large part of a newspaper or web page
senses.definitionCN: 把报道或照片铺满报纸版面或网页的大片区域
senses.example: The scandal was splashed across the front page.
senses.exampleCN: 那桩丑闻被铺满刊登在头版上。
senses.why: Ink and colour spread over a wide surface as a splash spreads over water, so print use borrows the verb.
senses.whyCN: 油墨和色彩在纸面上铺开，正如水花在水面上铺开，印刷用法因此借用了这个动词。

senses.title: To attract attention with an impression
senses.definition: to draw public attention by doing something noticeable or expensive
senses.definitionCN: 靠引人注目的举动或大笔花费引来公众关注
senses.example: The new brand made a splash with its first advert.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新品牌靠着第一支广告一举引起轰动。
senses.why: A loud splash on a calm surface draws every eye, and the phrase transfers that sudden attention to people.
senses.whyCN: 平静水面上的一声响亮水花会引来所有目光，习语把这种突然的注意转移到人身上。

intro.en: Splash is first recorded in English in the early eighteenth century and is probably imitative, built from the sound of something hitting water.
intro.cn: splash 在英语中首见于十八世纪初，一般认为属拟声词，由物体击水的声音构成，无可靠拉丁词根。

items.en: A reconstructed root with a pl- cluster for sudden wet impact may lie behind the word, but the reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 构拟形式认为存在一个以「pl」辅音群开头的日耳曼词根，表示突然的湿性撞击，但这一重构并不确定。

items.en: Similar imitative words such as plash and flash are already in use before splash appears.
items.cn: 在 splash 出现之前，plash 与 flash 这类拟声词已在英语中使用。

items.en: Splash is first recorded around this time, both as a verb and as a noun for flying water.
items.cn: 这一时期 splash 首次见于记载，既作动词，也作名词指飞溅的水。

items.en: The word spreads to colour, printing, and everyday phrases such as make a splash.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到颜色、印刷领域，并形成引起轰动等日常说法。

items.en: Splash now covers liquid, sound, colour, small amounts, publicity, and even the landing of space capsules.
items.cn: 现代英语中，splash 涵盖液体、声音、颜色、少量、宣传，甚至航天器的溅落。

note.en: Splash belongs to a sound-imitative family with plash and splatter, and sits near words for small airborne amounts of liquid.
note.cn: splash 与 plash、splatter 同属拟声家族，并与表示液体飞溅、洒落的一组词相邻。

entries.definition: to splash gently, or the light sound of water
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻溅水；潺潺水声，是更古老、更文雅的拟声同族词

entries.definition: to splash a thick liquid over a surface in drops
entries.definitionCN: 把稠液体溅得到处都是，与 splash 拼写相近、同属拟声词族

entries.definition: the landing of a spacecraft in the sea
entries.definitionCN: 航天器在海面上的溅落，由 splash 直接构成

entries.definition: liquid forced out in fine drops
entries.definitionCN: 喷出的细小液滴，颗粒更细、更均匀

entries.definition: to scatter drops of a thick liquid widely
entries.definitionCN: 使稠液体大范围溅落，强调弄脏的痕迹

entries.definition: to move your hands or feet about in water
entries.definitionCN: 用手或脚在水中嬉水，动作更轻、更小

normalIntro.en: Splash is a word you can almost hear: the pl sound arrives as something hits water and the drops fly.
normalIntro.cn: splash 几乎是一个能听见的词：有东西砸进水里、水滴飞起来的瞬间，「噗拉什」一声就来了。

normal.en: The hard pl cluster imitates a wet impact, as in plash and splatter.
normal.cn: 开头的 pl 辅音群模仿了湿性撞击声，plash 和 splatter 都是同理。

normal.en: Splash is both the action and the result, so you can make a splash and be in the splash.
normal.cn: splash 既是动作也是结果，既能说激起水花，也能说人在水花里。

normal.en: A splash of milk or of colour borrows the small audible drop as a unit.
normal.cn: 一点牛奶、一抹颜色都借用了「响一声」这个单位，所以量都很小。

normal.en: The fixed phrase make a splash transfers a loud water sound to public attention.
normal.cn: 固定短语 make a splash 把响亮的水声转用到公众关注上，即引起轰动。

normal.en: Compare spray: spray is fine and even, splash is big and scattered.
normal.cn: 对比 spray：spray 细而均匀，splash 大而散乱。

abstract.en: See a flat lake surface torn open by a falling stone.
abstract.cn: 想象平静的湖面被落石撕开，水花向上炸开。

abstract.en: Watch a hand fling water over a face and the drops scatter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把水往脸上甩，水珠四散。

abstract.en: Picture small boots jumping from puddle to puddle with a wet sound.
abstract.cn: 想象小靴子从一个水坑跳到下一个水坑，每一步都带水声。

examples.en: He splashed cold water on his face before the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会前他往脸上泼了冷水。

examples.en: The children laughed as they splashed about in the shallow stream.
examples.cn: 孩子们在浅溪里扑腾嬉水，笑得开心。

examples.en: She dropped the spoon into the sink with a splash.
examples.cn: 她把勺子掉进水槽，哗啦一声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死扑拉水」——跳进水里死命扑腾，水花四溅；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为属于拟声词，模仿物体猛然击水的声响，无可靠拉丁词根；同族的 plash、splatter 都保留了这一声音意象。

sensesIntro.en: Splash begins with the physical spray of a liquid, extends to the action, the sound, and the quantity, then spreads by image to colour, print, and public attention.
sensesIntro.cn: splash 从液体的实际飞溅出发，扩展到动作、声音与数量，再借意象延伸到颜色、印刷与公众关注。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone hitting water and drops bursting outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头击水，水珠向外炸开。

branches.en: The flying drops are the physical core of the word.
branches.cn: 飞溅的水滴是这个词语义的物理核心。

branches.en: Causing the spray and walking through water are the action senses.
branches.cn: 主动激起水花与蹚水行走是动作义项。

branches.en: The same event is heard as well as seen, which gives the sound sense.
branches.cn: 同一件事既可看见也可听见，于是产生声音义项。

branches.en: Colour and ink spreading over a surface reuse the visual image.
branches.cn: 颜色与油墨在表面上铺开，复用了这一视觉意象。

branches.en: One audible drop becomes a measure, and a loud one becomes attention.
branches.cn: 一声可听见的落水成为计量单位，一声巨响则成为公众注意。

intro.en: Splash is a monomorphemic imitative word; it has no productive Latin affixes, though the pl cluster links it to plash and splatter.
intro.cn: splash 是单语素拟声词，没有可用的拉丁词缀，但开头的 pl 辅音群把它与 plash、splatter 连成一族。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor: splash is an English imitative coinage, so the Latin family list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: splash 没有拉丁语祖先，是英语自造的拟声词，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Plash is the older, gentler cousin of splash.
items.exampleCN: plash 是 splash 更古老、更轻柔的亲戚。

items.meaning: to throw liquid into the air
items.example: Splash imitates the sound of the impact.
items.exampleCN: splash 模仿了撞击的声响。

items.meaning: one who or that which does something
items.meaningCN: 表示动作发出者的后缀
items.example: The suffix -er forms splasher.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 splasher。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y forms splashy from splash.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 splash 变成 splashy。

items.example: Splatter shares the pl sound with splash.
items.exampleCN: splatter 与 splash 共享 pl 音。

items.meaning: to scatter small drops on something
items.example: Spatter is the smaller-scale partner of splash.
items.exampleCN: spatter 是 splash 规模更小的搭档。

items.example: The adverb down forms splashdown.
items.exampleCN: 副词 down 构成 splashdown。

items.example: The noun back forms splashback.
items.exampleCN: 名词 back 构成 splashback。

items.meaning: a spacecraft landing in the sea
items.example: Splashdown reuses the drops from a landing.
items.exampleCN: splashdown 复用了落水溅起的水滴意象。

definition_zh: 夹板；木片；护腿甲片
definition_en: a long thin piece of wood or plastic used to keep a broken bone still, or a thin split strip of wood
core_image: 两块细木片夹住受伤的手臂，再用布条一圈圈缠紧
scene: 登山者摔断了手腕，同伴用树枝和围巾给他做了个临时夹板。The climber broke his wrist, so his partner made a rough splint from a stick and a scarf.
sceneCN: 这里 splint 是「夹板」（第 1 个义项：固定断骨的长条硬片）；句意：登山者摔断了手腕，同伴用树枝和围巾给他做了个临时夹板。

derivatives.zh: 木刺；碎片；与 splint 同源，由窄木片引申为扎手的碎屑
夹板固定术；splint 加 -ing 表示这一医疗操作
用夹板固定的；splint 加 -ed 作定语

senses.title: A strip used to hold a broken bone
senses.definition: a thin rigid strip, often of wood, placed alongside a limb to keep a broken bone still
senses.definitionCN: 放在肢体旁、用来固定断骨的细长硬片，多为木质
senses.example: The nurse put a splint on his broken finger.
senses.exampleCN: 护士给他的断指打上了夹板。
senses.why: The original object is a split-off strip of wood, and in medicine that rigid strip became a tool for holding a bone still.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指劈下来的一条木片，在医学里这条硬木片被用来把骨头固定住，于是成了夹板。

senses.title: To fix a body part with a splint
senses.definition: to support or hold a damaged body part in place with a rigid strip
senses.definitionCN: 用硬片把受伤的部位支撑固定在原位
senses.example: The doctor splinted the leg before the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在出发前给那条腿上了夹板。
senses.why: Naming the object easily turns into naming the action of fitting it, so the noun gave rise to a verb.
senses.whyCN: 物品有了名字，安放它的动作就顺理成章地也用了这个词，名词于是长出了动词。

senses.title: A thin split piece of wood
senses.definition: a thin narrow strip split from a larger piece of wood
senses.definitionCN: 从大块木料上劈下或撕下的细窄长条
senses.example: He wove the basket from splints of willow.
senses.exampleCN: 他用柳木条编成了篮子。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the word is simply a long thin piece split off from wood, before any medical use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的义项就是木条劈下来的一块长条，在医学用途出现之前就已存在。

senses.title: A plate in a suit of armour
senses.definition: an overlapping plate or strip of armour worn over the leg
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在腿部的相互叠压的铠甲片或条
senses.example: The knight strapped the steel splints to his shins.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士把钢制甲片绑在小腿上。
senses.why: Armour was made of narrow overlapping strips like wooden splints, so the shape sense carried over to metal plates.
senses.whyCN: 铠甲由一条条相互叠压的窄片制成，正像木夹板，于是形状义延伸到了金属甲片。

senses.title: A piece of wood for a dog to carry
senses.definition: a small strip of wood, especially one put in a dog mouth to be carried in a field trial
senses.definitionCN: 小块木片，尤指放进狗嘴里让它叼着以完成猎犬测试的木件
senses.example: The handler gave the spaniel a wooden splint to retrieve.
senses.exampleCN: 训犬员给那只猎犬一块木片让它叼回。
senses.why: Hunters needed a light object a dog could carry in its mouth, and a wooden strip suited the job perfectly.
senses.whyCN: 猎人需要一个能被狗叼住的轻便物件，一条薄木片恰好合用。

senses.title: A bar in coal mining
senses.definition: a short bar of wood used to brace or line a shaft in a mine
senses.definitionCN: 矿井里用来支撑或衬垫坑道的短木条
senses.example: The miners wedged splints between the roof beams.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工在顶梁之间楔上木条加固。
senses.why: Miners reused split-off wood strips to shore up tunnels, so the basic wood-strip sense turned technical.
senses.whyCN: 矿工把劈下来的木条拿来撑住坑道，于是基本的木条义变成了行话。

intro.en: Splint comes from Middle Dutch splinte or Middle Low German splinte, a thin strip of wood or metal split off from a larger piece.
intro.cn: splint 来自中古荷兰语 splinte 或中古低地德语 splinte，指从大块材料上劈下的细长木片或金属片。

items.en: A root meaning to split or to come apart lies behind the word, but its exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 词根一般认为表示劈开、裂开，但确切构拟形式不确定。

items.en: Splinte names a thin strip split from wood or metal, a meaning still visible today.
items.cn: splinte 指从木头或金属上劈下的细长条，这个含义今天仍能看出。

items.en: Splint enters English as the name for such a split strip.
items.cn: splint 进入英语，最初就指这种劈下来的木条。

items.en: The word is applied to armour plates and to the strips that brace a broken limb.
items.cn: 这个词开始用于铠甲片，以及用来固定伤肢的木条。

items.en: Medical use settles into the modern meaning of a rigid support for a fracture.
items.cn: 医学用法逐渐固定为现代含义，即固定骨折的硬质支撑物。

note.en: Splint belongs to a small family of split-wood words, and heads a medical field with cast, brace, and crutch.
note.cn: splint 属于表示「劈开的木片」的一个小词族，并与石膏、护具、拐杖同处一个医疗义场。

entries.definition: a small sharp piece broken off wood or glass
entries.definitionCN: 从木头或玻璃上崩下的细小尖片，与 splint 同源

entries.definition: supported with a splint
entries.definitionCN: 用夹板固定住的，是 splint 的形容词形式

entries.definition: one of two small leg bones in horses
entries.definitionCN: 马的腿部小骨，因其细长形似木条而得名，与夹板同词不同义

entries.definition: a hard shell that holds a broken bone in place
entries.definitionCN: 包住骨折处的硬质石膏，比夹板包裹更完整

entries.definition: a support worn on the body to hold it firm
entries.definitionCN: 穿戴在身体上起固定作用的护具

entries.definition: a strip of cloth used to bind a wound
entries.definitionCN: 包扎伤口的布条，只做缠绕不做硬支撑

normalIntro.en: Splint carries a split-inside taste: it began as a strip split off from wood and was later strapped to a broken bone.
normalIntro.cn: splint 带着「劈开」的味道：它原是木头上劈下来的一条，后来被绑到断骨上。

normal.en: Splint and splinter share a root, and a splinter is what a splint once could break into.
normal.cn: splint 与 splinter 同源，splinter 正是木夹板可能崩下的小碎刺。

normal.en: The fixed phrase in a splint describes a limb that cannot move.
normal.cn: 固定说法 in a splint 描述一条动弹不得的肢体。

normal.en: Splints of willow means strips of willow used for weaving.
normal.cn: splints of willow 指用来编织的柳木条。

normal.en: As a noun and a verb, splint covers both the strip and the act of strapping it on.
normal.cn: splint 既是名词又是动词，既指木片本身，也指把它绑上去的动作。

normal.en: Compare cast: a cast wraps the whole limb, a splint is a rigid strip alongside it.
normal.cn: 对比 cast：石膏包住整条肢体，夹板只是贴在旁边的硬片。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden board laid beside a swollen arm and tied with strips of cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木板贴在肿胀的手臂旁，用布条一圈圈绑紧。

abstract.en: See a long strip peeling off a plank as the knife goes down.
abstract.cn: 想象刀顺着木板上往下走，一条长木片被剖下来。

abstract.en: Imagine a knot that keeps an injured limb frozen until it heals.
abstract.cn: 想象一个结把受伤的肢体冻结住，直到它长好。

examples.en: His arm was kept in a splint for several weeks.
examples.cn: 他的手臂打了几周夹板。

examples.en: The paramedics splinted the leg on the roadside.
examples.cn: 急救人员在路边给那条腿上了夹板。

examples.en: Thin splints of oak were woven into the basket.
examples.cn: 细橡木条被编进了篮子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「四平」——把小木条贴得四平八稳，把断骨牢牢固定住；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古荷兰语 splinte（从木料上劈下的细长片）→ 英语 splint（木条；夹板），同源词 splinter 保留了「碎裂木刺」的含义。

sensesIntro.en: Splint starts as a strip split from wood, then moves through armour plates and mining bars to the medical sense that now dominates.
sensesIntro.cn: splint 从「劈下的木条」出发，经过甲片与矿井木条，最后落到今天占主导地位的夹板义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow wooden strip strapped along a limb.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条窄木片沿着肢体绑紧。

branches.en: The bare split strip of wood is the oldest and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 劈开的木条是最古老、最字面的义项。

branches.en: The medical splint is the same strip used to hold bone still.
branches.cn: 医疗夹板就是同一种木条，用来把骨头固定住。

branches.en: The treatment sense is the verb that grew out of the object.
branches.cn: 治疗义项是由物件生长出来的动词。

branches.en: Armour and mine supports reuse the strip as a structural element.
branches.cn: 铠甲与矿井支架把木条改写为结构构件。

branches.en: Both the splint and the wooden object for a dog are pieces put against or into the body.
branches.cn: 医疗夹板与给狗叼的木片，都是贴住或放进身体部位的物件。

intro.en: Splint is a whole Germanic loan with no productive affixes of its own, though the family of split-words around it is large.
intro.cn: splint 是完整的日耳曼语借词，本身没有可拆的后缀，但它周围的「劈开」词族很庞大。

latinIntro.en: Splint has no Latin ancestor; it comes from Middle Dutch, so the Latin family list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: splint 没有拉丁语祖先，来自中古荷兰语，因此拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Splint names a strip split off wood.
items.exampleCN: splint 指从木料上劈下的一条。

items.example: Splinter keeps the breaking image of the root.
items.exampleCN: splinter 保留了词根的碎裂意象。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms splinted.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 splinted。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或过程的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms splinting.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 splinting。

items.example: The noun bone forms splint bone.
items.exampleCN: 名词 bone 构成 splint bone。

items.example: Wood splinters when hit by an axe.
items.exampleCN: 木头被斧子砍中时会裂成细片。

items.meaning: to cut downwards in a line
items.example: Split supplies the core image of separating wood.
items.exampleCN: split 提供了把木头分开的核心意象。

items.meaning: to hold with a rigid strip
items.example: Nurses can splint a finger quickly.
items.exampleCN: 护士能迅速给手指上夹板。

definition_zh: 腐坏；变质；腐坏变质的食品；损耗
definition_en: the process or state of food or goods going bad, or the amount lost in this way
core_image: 冰箱断电一夜，牛奶胀袋、水果长毛，整托盘食物被倒进垃圾桶
scene: 夏天高温下，冷库里的鲜虾迅速变质，损失惨重。In the summer heat the prawns in the cold store suffered rapid spoilage and the loss was heavy.
sceneCN: 这里 spoilage 是「腐坏、变质」（第 1 个义项：食品变坏的过程）；句意：夏天高温下，冷库里的鲜虾迅速变质，损失惨重。

derivatives.zh: 使变坏；破坏；宠坏；是 spoilage 的基础动词
变质的；被宠坏的；spoil 加 -ed 构成
战利品；分得的赃物；spoil 加 -s 的复数名词
未受破坏的；原来完好的；un- 加 spoiled

senses.title: The process of food going bad
senses.definition: the process by which food or drink becomes unfit to eat or drink
senses.definitionCN: 食品或饮料变得不能吃、不能喝的过程
senses.example: Keep the meat cool to slow spoilage.
senses.exampleCN: 把肉冷藏起来以减缓变质。
senses.why: The verb spoil means to go bad, and the noun suffix -age turns the action into the process itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词 spoil 意为变坏，名词后缀 -age 把动作变成了过程本身，于是有了腐坏这个义项。

senses.title: Food that has already gone bad
senses.definition: food or other perishable goods that are too old or damaged to be sold or eaten
senses.definitionCN: 已经过期或损坏、不能出售也不能食用的食品及易腐货物
senses.example: The kitchen returns spoilage to the supplier every week.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房每周都把变质食品退回给供应商。
senses.why: The uncountable process sense easily shifts to naming what results from it, namely the ruined goods themselves.
senses.whyCN: 不可数的过程义很容易转指它造成的结果，也就是那些已经坏掉的东西。

senses.title: Loss caused by goods going bad
senses.definition: the amount of stock or money lost because goods deteriorate before being used
senses.definitionCN: 货物在使用前就已变质而损失的数量或金额
senses.example: The report tracks spoilage in the supermarket chain.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告追踪连锁超市里的腐坏损耗。
senses.why: In business, every bad item is a quantifiable loss, so the noun turns into an accounting category.
senses.whyCN: 在商业里，每一件坏掉的货都是可量化的损失，所以这个词变成了会计术语。

senses.title: Paper going yellow and brittle
senses.definition: the gradual decay of paper, often in old books, caused by acid and light
senses.definitionCN: 由酸性物质和光照导致的老书纸张逐渐发黄变脆
senses.example: Acid in cheap paper speeds up spoilage.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价纸张里的酸会加快纸张老化。
senses.why: Anything that was once good and slowly turns useless is spoiled, so the word extends from food to paper.
senses.whyCN: 凡是原本完好、慢慢变得无用的东西都算被毁，而这个词因此从食品延伸到纸张。

senses.title: A defect found in castings
senses.definition: a flaw in a cast metal part that makes it unusable
senses.definitionCN: 铸造金属件中使其不能使用的瑕疵
senses.example: The foundry checks each part for spoilage.
senses.exampleCN: 铸造厂逐个检查零件有没有缺陷。
senses.why: Manufacturing borrowed the same idea of a finished product being ruined before use.
senses.whyCN: 制造业借用了同一个观念：成品在派上用场之前就已经毁掉。

senses.title: Something becoming worthless
senses.definition: the state of something losing its value or being ruined
senses.definitionCN: 事物失去价值或被毁坏的状态
senses.example: Rapid spoilage of ideas is common in fashion.
senses.exampleCN: 在时尚界，理念迅速失去价值是很常见的。
senses.why: The most abstract branch keeps only the sense of worth being drained away.
senses.whyCN: 最抽象的分支只保留了价值被掏空这一层意思。

intro.en: Spoilage is an English formation of the verb spoil plus the noun suffix -age, from Old French espoillier, to strip or plunder.
intro.cn: spoilage 是英语用动词 spoil 加名词后缀 -age 构成的词，其源头为古法语 espoillier（剥取、掠夺）。

items.en: Spoillier descends from Latin spoliare, to strip someone or take their goods.
items.cn: espoillier 源自拉丁语 spoliare，意为剥掉某人的东西、夺取财物。

items.en: Espoillier keeps the sense of stripping and plundering.
items.cn: espoillier 保留了剥取与掠夺的含义。

items.en: Spoil enters English meaning to strip, plunder, or take by force.
items.cn: spoil 进入英语，义为剥夺、掠夺、强夺。

items.en: The sense weakens from outright plunder to making something bad or useless.
items.cn: 词义从明火抢掠减弱为把事情弄坏、弄得没用。

items.en: Spoilage is coined with -age to name the process of goods going bad.
items.cn: 加 -age 构成 spoilage，用来表示货物变坏的过程。

items.en: Spoilage is now chiefly technical, used in food science, retail, and printing.
items.cn: 现代英语中 spoilage 主要用于专业领域，如食品科学、零售与印刷。

note.en: Spoilage is the -age noun of spoil, and sits with decay, decomposition, and rot as words for things going bad.
note.cn: spoilage 是 spoil 加 -age 构成的名词，与 decay、decomposition、rot 一同表示东西坏掉。

entries.definition: to make food or a plan go bad
entries.definitionCN: 使食物变坏或使计划落空，是 spoilage 的基础动词

entries.definition: bad or ruined, especially of food or a child
entries.definitionCN: 变坏的、被宠坏的，是 spoil 的形容词形式

entries.definition: goods taken by force or won in a contest
entries.definitionCN: 战利品、得手之物，来自同一个词但含义已不同

entries.definition: the gradual destruction of material by bacteria or nature
entries.definitionCN: 由细菌或自然作用逐渐造成的分解腐烂

entries.definition: the breaking down of organic matter
entries.definitionCN: 有机物分解为简单成分的过程，更偏科学术语

entries.definition: the state of becoming soft and rotten
entries.definitionCN: 变软、烂掉的状态，更强调腐烂本身

normalIntro.en: Spoilage is spoil turned into a noun: whatever spoil does over time is spoilage.
normalIntro.cn: spoilage 就是 spoil 变名词：一切随时间坏掉的过程都叫 spoilage。

normal.en: The suffix -age turns an action into a process, as in drain to drainage.
normal.cn: 后缀 -age 把动作变成过程，比如从 drain 到 drainage。

normal.en: Spoil once meant to plunder, so spoilage still carries the idea of goods being stripped away.
normal.cn: spoil 原义为掠夺，因此 spoilage 仍带有货物被夺走的意思。

normal.en: In retail, spoilage is a countable loss reported in the accounts.
normal.cn: 在零售业，spoilage 是一种记在账上的可量化损耗。

normal.en: Food spoilage is the most common collocation and the safest one to use.
normal.cn: food spoilage 是最常见也最稳妥的搭配。

normal.en: Compare rot, which is the physical rotting, with spoilage, which is the whole process and loss.
normal.cn: 对比 rot：rot 是物理上的烂，spoilage 则涵盖整个过程与损失。

abstract.en: Picture a fridge that stops working overnight and milk that swells in its carton.
abstract.cn: 想象冰柜夜里断电，牛奶在纸盒里胀了起来。

abstract.en: See a market worker dumping a crate of soft tomatoes into a bin.
abstract.cn: 想象市场里的人把一箱烂软的番茄倒进垃圾桶。

abstract.en: Imagine a ledger line where spilled money is recorded as spoilage.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上有一行，把白扔的钱记作腐坏损耗。

examples.en: Proper packaging can greatly reduce spoilage during transport.
examples.cn: 合适的包装能大幅减少运输过程中的腐坏。

examples.en: Bacteria are the main cause of spoilage in dairy products.
examples.cn: 细菌是乳制品变质的主要原因。

examples.en: The restaurant lowers its spoilage rate by ordering fresh meat daily.
examples.cn: 这家餐厅每天采购新鲜肉类，以降低损耗率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 spoil 加 age，东西熬老了」——任何东西只要存放得太久，就熬成了坏掉的状态；这只是拆词谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 spoliare（剥夺、抢夺）→ 古法语 espoillier（掠夺）→ 英语 spoil（剥去；弄坏）→ 加 -age 构成 spoilage，核心义从「夺走」滑向「好物被夺、变得无用」。

sensesIntro.en: Spoilage moves from the process of food going bad, to the bad goods, to the loss they cause, and finally to any value being ruined.
sensesIntro.cn: spoilage 从食品变坏的过程，扩展到坏掉的货、它们造成的损失，最后泛指任何价值的丧失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: good food left too long and turning worthless.
core.cn: 核心意象：原本完好的食物放得太久，变得一文不值。

branches.en: The core process of food going bad is the primary sense.
branches.cn: 食品变坏的过程是首要义项。

branches.en: What the process produces is bad food itself.
branches.cn: 这个过程的结果就是已经坏掉的食物本身。

branches.en: Money lost to the process becomes an accounting term.
branches.cn: 因这一过程损失的钱款成了会计术语。

branches.en: Paper and metal castings go bad in the same way, so the word enters materials and industry.
branches.cn: 纸张与金属铸件以同样方式变坏，这个词由此进入材料与工业领域。

branches.en: The most abstract branch keeps only the draining away of value.
branches.cn: 最抽象的分支只留下价值被掏空这一点。

intro.en: Spoilage is built from the English verb spoil and the productive suffix -age, with spoil itself coming from Latin spoliare.
intro.cn: spoilage 由英语动词 spoil 与能产后缀 -age 构成，而 spoil 本身来自拉丁语 spoliare。

latinIntro.en: Latin spoliare means to strip or plunder, and the noun spolium means the stripped hide or the spoils.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spoliare 意为剥取、抢夺，名词 spolium 指剥下来的兽皮或战利品。

items.example: Spoil is the base that spoilage is built on.
items.exampleCN: spoil 是构成 spoilage 的基础词。

items.meaningCN: 表示过程、动作或数量的后缀
items.example: The suffix -age turns spoil into spoilage.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 把 spoil 变成 spoilage。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms spoiled.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 spoiled。

items.example: The suffix -s forms spoils.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -s 构成 spoils。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unspoiled.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unspoiled。

items.example: Food combines with spoilage as food spoilage.
items.exampleCN: food 与 spoilage 组成 food spoilage。

items.meaning: the flow or removal of water
items.example: Drainage shows the same -age process pattern.
items.exampleCN: drainage 展示了同样的 -age 过程构词。

items.example: Spoiled food must not be sold.
items.exampleCN: 变质食品不得出售。

latinEntries.meaning: to rob or strip of something
the destruction of evidence or goods
latinEntries.meaningCN: 毁损证据或财物，主要用于法律

definition_zh: 海绵；海绵块；抹布；用海绵擦；白吃白用
definition_en: a soft light material full of holes that soaks up water, or a piece of it used for washing and cleaning
core_image: 一块布满小孔的海绵，一按就吸满水
scene: 厨房水槽边放着一块湿海绵，洗碗时随手就用它吸水擦洗。The kitchen sink has a damp sponge beside it for washing the dishes.
sceneCN: 这里 sponge 是「海绵块、洗碗布」（第 1 个义项：吸水的清洁用具）；句意：厨房水槽边放着一块湿海绵，用来洗碗。

derivatives.zh: 由 sponge 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「海绵似的、松软多孔的」
由 sponge 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「靠别人养活的人、寄生虫」
由 sponge 与拉丁词根 -form（形状）合成，义为「海绵状的」

senses.title: A soft porous material
senses.definition: a soft, light material with many small holes, natural or man-made, that can absorb liquid
senses.definitionCN: 一种柔软轻巧、布满小孔的材料，天然或人造都有，能吸收液体
senses.example: Natural sponge is still sold for washing cars.
senses.exampleCN: 天然海绵至今仍被出售，用来洗车。
senses.why: The Greek and Latin names describe a sea animal whose soft, sieve-like body soaks up water, so the material took its name from the creature.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语和拉丁语里的名称指一种身体柔软似筛、能吸水的海洋生物，这种材料的名字便直接借自那种生物。

senses.title: Something used for washing
senses.definition: a piece of this material, often with an abrasive side, used with water and soap for cleaning
senses.definitionCN: 一块这种材料，常带一面粗糙层，蘸水加肥皂用来清洗东西
senses.example: Wipe the table with a damp sponge.
senses.exampleCN: 用湿海绵把桌子擦一遍。
senses.why: Once the material exists, the object that holds water and scrubs a surface becomes its most everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 材料一旦存在，用来含水和擦洗表面的那个物件就成了它最日常的义项。

senses.title: To wipe with a sponge
senses.definition: to clean or wipe a surface, or to remove liquid, using a sponge
senses.definitionCN: 用海绵把表面擦净，或把液体吸去
senses.example: She sponged the coffee off the tablecloth.
senses.exampleCN: 她用海绵把桌布上的咖啡擦掉。
senses.why: The noun easily turns into a verb for what the object does: absorbing and wiping in the same motion.
senses.whyCN: 名词很自然地转成动词，指这个物件本身的动作：一边吸水一边擦，同一个动作完成。

senses.title: To live at someone else expense
senses.definition: to get money, food, or other things from someone without giving anything in return
senses.definitionCN: 不付出任何东西，却从别人那里得到钱、食物或其他好处
senses.example: He has been sponging off his parents for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他多年来一直靠父母养活。
senses.why: A sponge soaks up whatever liquid is around without giving it back, so a person who absorbs another person money is called a sponge.
senses.whyCN: 海绵把周围的水全吸走却不还回去，于是只知道从别人身上吸取好处的人也被叫作 sponge。

senses.title: A type of light cake
senses.definition: a light cake made with eggs, sugar, and flour, full of small air holes
senses.definitionCN: 用鸡蛋、糖和面粉做成的轻盈蛋糕，内部布满小气孔
senses.example: She baked a lemon sponge for tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她烤了一个柠檬海绵蛋糕配茶。
senses.why: The fine network of air holes looks just like the holes in a sponge, so the cake borrowed the name.
senses.whyCN: 蛋糕内部细密的气孔网络看起来和海绵的孔洞一模一样，于是蛋糕也借用了这个名字。

intro.en: Sponge comes from Greek spongos or sphongos, a sea animal, and the word first entered English through Latin and Old French forms.
intro.cn: sponge 来自希腊语 spongos 或 sphongos，原本指一种海洋生物，经拉丁语和古法语形式进入英语。

items.en: Spongos named a sponge animal used for cleaning and as a symbol in Greek shrines.
items.cn: spongos 指一种海绵动物，可用来擦洗，也出现在希腊神庙的器物意象中。

items.en: Latin spongia borrowed the Greek word for the sea animal and its dried skeleton.
items.cn: 拉丁语 spongia 借入这个希腊词，既指这种海洋生物，也指它干燥后的骨架。

items.en: The word reached English in forms like sponge and sponge, describing the animal first.
items.cn: 这个词以 sponge 等写法的前身进入英语，最初仍指这种生物。

items.en: Sponge settled as the spelling for both the sea animal and the material cut from it.
items.cn: 到中古英语，sponge 的拼写稳定下来，既指海绵动物，也指从它取下的材料。

items.en: The verb sponge developed from washing and wiping, and by the nineteenth century it also meant living off others.
items.cn: 动词用法从擦洗和吸水发展而来，到十九世纪又表示靠他人生活。

note.en: Sponge sits at the heart of a small family of absorbing and porous words, and is close to everyday cleaning and soaking terms.
note.cn: sponge 位于「吸水、多孔」这一小词族的中心，与日常的清洁和浸泡词义相邻。

entries.definition: soft and full of small holes, like a sponge
entries.definitionCN: 柔软多孔的，像海绵一样

entries.definition: a person who lives off other people
entries.definitionCN: 靠别人养活的人；寄生虫

entries.definition: shaped like a sponge, used in medical terms
entries.definitionCN: 海绵状的，常用于医学术语

entries.definition: a small piece of material used for wiping or cleaning
entries.definitionCN: 用于擦拭或清洁的小块材料

entries.definition: a tool with a soft head for cleaning floors
entries.definitionCN: 带软头的拖把；用来擦洗的工具

entries.definition: a rough pad used for scrubbing pans
entries.definitionCN: 擦洗锅具用的粗糙擦洗垫

normalIntro.en: Sponge is a family of holes: the material, the washing block, the wiping verb, the freeloader, and the airy cake.
normalIntro.cn: sponge 是一族「孔洞」：吸水材料、洗碗工具、擦拭动作、白吃白用的人、以及多孔轻盈的蛋糕。

normal.en: Sponge and spongy share the same root: something soft with many holes is spongy.
