normal.cn: sponge 与 spongy 同根：柔软又多孔的东西就是 spongy。

normal.en: A sponge cake is named for its air holes, not for washing.
normal.cn: sponge cake 得名于它的气孔，而不是因为用来洗东西。

normal.en: To sponge up water is to absorb it, a meaning that spilled over into sponging off money.
normal.cn: sponge up water 是吸水，这个意思进而延伸到 sponge off 别人的钱。

normal.en: Sponger adds a person suffix to sponge: one who absorbs other people resources.
normal.cn: sponger 在 sponge 后加表示人的后缀，指吸取别人资源的人。

normal.en: Sponge bath uses the object with water and soap, so the cleaning sense is always there.
normal.cn: sponge bath 用水和肥皂配合海绵使用，清洁义始终在场。

abstract.en: Press a sponge and watch the water run out, then squeeze it back in.
abstract.cn: 按下海绵看水被挤出，再把水吸回去。

abstract.en: Picture a counter wiped clean of crumbs with one smooth stroke.
abstract.cn: 想象用海绵一下把台面上的碎屑擦净。

abstract.en: Think of someone drinking a free coffee while others pay for it.
abstract.cn: 想象有人喝着免费的咖啡，账单却由别人来付。

examples.en: Squeeze the sponge and put it back in the sink.
examples.cn: 把海绵挤干，放回水槽里。

examples.en: He sponged the spilled milk off the floor.
examples.cn: 他用海绵把洒在地板上的牛奶吸干。

examples.en: The children shared a slice of sponge after lunch.
examples.cn: 午饭后孩子们分吃了一块海绵蛋糕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯胖吉」：吃完一肚子东西还越泡越胖的，是白吃白用的寄生者，也是泡水就鼓起来的海绵。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 spongos 或 sphongos（海绵动物）→ 拉丁语 spongia → 古法语 sponge 形式 → 中古英语 sponge，核心义「能吸水的多孔物」。

sensesIntro.en: Sponge begins with the absorbent sea material, then moves to the washing object, the wiping verb, the freeloader, and the airy cake.
sensesIntro.cn: sponge 先指能吸水的海绵材料，再指用来擦洗的海绵块、擦拭的动词、白吃白用的人和轻盈多孔的蛋糕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a soft block full of tiny holes that drinks up water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块布满小孔、能把水吸进去的柔软物。

branches.en: The porous sea material is the direct source sense.
branches.cn: 多孔的海洋材料是最贴近词源的义项。

branches.en: The washing block and the wiping action are the same everyday scene seen as thing and verb.
branches.cn: 洗碗海绵与擦拭动作是同一个日常场景，一个作名词一个作动词。

branches.en: The freeloader is the abstract transfer: absorbing without giving back.
branches.cn: 白吃白用是抽象转移：只吸收，不回报。

branches.en: The cake borrows the name from its network of small air holes.
branches.cn: 蛋糕因其细密气孔的网络而得名。

branches.en: The shared thread is absorbing and holding liquid inside many holes.
branches.cn: 共同的线索是在众多孔洞里吸附并保存液体。

intro.en: Sponge is an old borrowed noun, with English spongy and sponger built around it and the technical compound spongiform in medicine.
intro.cn: sponge 是早期借入的古老名词，英语围绕它构成 spongy 与 sponger，医学里还有复合词 spongiform。

latinIntro.en: Latin spongia comes from Greek spongos, a word for the sea animal, and also named its dried skeleton.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spongia 来自希腊语 spongos，指那种海洋生物，也指它干燥后的骨架。

items.meaning: a sea animal with a porous body
items.example: Spongos is the Greek source of the borrowing.
items.exampleCN: spongos 是那个希腊源词。

items.meaning: a sponge, both the animal and its skeleton
items.example: Latin spongia carried the word westward.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 spongia 把词带向西方。

items.meaning: a soft porous material that absorbs water
items.meaningCN: 柔软多孔、能吸水的材料
items.example: A sponge is handy in the kitchen.
items.exampleCN: 海绵在厨房里很好用。

items.meaning: to wipe or absorb with a sponge
items.example: Sponge the stain before it dries.
items.exampleCN: 趁污渍未干赶紧用海绵吸掉。

items.example: The suffix -y forms spongy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 spongy。

items.example: The ground was spongy after the rain.
items.exampleCN: 雨后地面松软多孔。

items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人的词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms sponger.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 sponger。

items.meaning: a person who lives off others
items.example: Nobody wants to be called a sponger.
items.exampleCN: 谁都不想被叫作寄生虫。

items.example: The combining form -form forms spongiform.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -form 构成 spongiform。

items.example: Spongiform appears in medical writing.
items.exampleCN: spongiform 常见于医学写作。

latinEntries.meaning: full of holes like a sponge

definition_zh: 赞助；资助；赞助权；发起人身份
definition_en: money or support given to an event, activity, or person by a company or other backer
core_image: 活动背景板上并排印着赞助商的名字
scene: 马拉松赛道的拱门上印着几家公司的标识，说明这场比赛的资金来自它们。The race arch carried several company logos, a sign of their sponsorship of the event.
sceneCN: 这里 sponsorship 是「赞助、资助」（第 1 个义项：为活动出钱支持）；句意：拱门上印着几家公司的标识，显示它们赞助了这场比赛。

derivatives.zh: sponsorship 的基础词，义为「赞助商、赞助者」
由 sponsor 加过去分词词尾 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「受赞助的、赞助性的」
由 sponsor 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为「赞助商的、由赞助构成的」

senses.title: Financial support for an activity
senses.definition: money or support that a company, group, or person gives to an event, activity, or project
senses.definitionCN: 公司、团体或个人为活动、项目提供的资金或支持
senses.example: The festival is funded by local sponsorship.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆由本地赞助提供资金。
senses.why: The Latin root promises something on behalf of the person who speaks, and a sponsor today keeps that promise with money, so sponsorship is the whole arrangement of giving support.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为替他人郑重承诺，今天的赞助商就是用钱来兑现承诺，所以 sponsorship 指整个提供支持的安排。

senses.title: A sponsorship arrangement or deal
senses.definition: a formal agreement under which someone pays to support an event or person, usually in return for publicity
senses.definitionCN: 一方出资支持活动或个人的正式协议，通常以宣传曝光为回报
senses.example: The athlete signed a sponsorship with a sportswear brand.
senses.exampleCN: 这名运动员与一家运动品牌签了赞助合同。
senses.why: Once a promise of money becomes a written deal, the noun can name the contract rather than the money.
senses.whyCN: 一旦出钱的承诺变成书面协议，这个名词就能指合同本身，而不再只指那笔钱。

senses.title: The position of a sponsor
senses.definition: the status or role of a person who formally proposes or backs a plan, law, or proposal
senses.definitionCN: 正式提出或支持计划、法律、提案的人所处的身份或角色
senses.example: She has taken over the sponsorship of the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 她接手成为这项法案的发起人。
senses.why: Because the base word also means the person who puts a proposal forward, the suffix -ship extends it to the role itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为基础词也指「提出提案的人」，后缀 -ship 便把它延伸为那份身份与职责。

senses.title: Backing a person or institution
senses.titleCN: 对个人或机构的资助、扶持
senses.definition: support given to a person, team, or institution so that it can work, study, or train
senses.definitionCN: 给予个人、团队或机构的支持，使其能工作、学习或训练
senses.example: The scholarship offers sponsorship for three years of study.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金提供三年的学习资助。
senses.why: The same promise of support applies to people rather than events, covering study, work, and training.
senses.whyCN: 同一种支持的承诺也可以落到人而不是活动上，涵盖学习、工作和培训。

intro.en: Sponsorship combines sponsor, from Latin spondere, to promise solemnly, with the English suffix -ship, meaning state or condition.
intro.cn: sponsorship 由 sponsor 与英语后缀 -ship 组合而成，前者源自拉丁语 spondere（郑重承诺），后者表示身份或状况。

items.en: Spondere meant to promise in a formal, binding way, often on behalf of another.
items.cn: spondere 意为正式而有约束力地承诺，常是替他人许诺。

items.en: Sponsor named a person who makes such a pledge, and sponsio the pledge itself.
items.cn: sponsor 指作出这种承诺的人，sponsio 指承诺本身。

items.en: The idea of a surety or godparent entered English through church and legal Latin.
items.cn: 保人与教父母这类角色经教会与法律拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Sponsor was used for a person who answers for another at baptism.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，sponsor 用于指洗礼时替他人作保的人。

items.en: Commercial sponsoring of sport and events gave the base word new life.
items.cn: 体育与活动的商业赞助赋予这个词新的生命。

items.en: The suffix -ship turned the backer into the backing, the state and arrangement of sponsoring.
items.cn: 后缀 -ship 把赞助者转变为赞助行为，即支持的状态与安排。

note.en: Sponsorship belongs to the sponsor family and to the small group of abstract nouns in -ship, and it borders on funding and backing words.
note.cn: sponsorship 属于 sponsor 词族，也在以 -ship 结尾的抽象名词小类中，并与出资、支持类词相邻。

entries.definition: a person or company that pays for an event
entries.definitionCN: 为活动出资的个人或公司

entries.definition: paid for or supported by a sponsor
relating to a sponsor
the state of working together
entries.definitionCN: 合作伙伴关系，共用 -ship 后缀

entries.definition: support given by a wealthy or powerful person
entries.definitionCN: 有钱或有势者的资助与支持

entries.definition: money provided for a project or activity
entries.definitionCN: 为项目或活动提供的资金

entries.definition: support, often financial, for a plan or person
entries.definitionCN: 对计划或个人的支持，常指资金支持

normalIntro.en: Sponsorship is a promise made concrete: sponsor plus -ship names the money, the deal, the role, and long-term backing.
normalIntro.cn: sponsorship 是落到实处的承诺：sponsor 加 -ship，同时指那笔钱、那份合同、那个身份和长期资助。

normal.en: Sponsor goes back to Latin spondere, to promise, so a sponsorship is a promise of support.
normal.cn: sponsor 可追溯到拉丁语 spondere（承诺），所以 sponsorship 就是支持他人的承诺。

normal.en: The suffix -ship turns a person into a state or arrangement, as in friendship and partnership.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ship 把「人」变成「状态或安排」，friendship 与 partnership 都是如此。

normal.en: Corporate sponsorship is the most common phrase: a company pays and gets its logo shown.
normal.cn: corporate sponsorship 是最常见的搭配：公司出钱，换来品牌标识的展示。

normal.en: A sponsorship deal is the written form of the promise.
normal.cn: sponsorship deal 是这份承诺的书面形式。

normal.en: Spontaneous looks similar but comes from a different Latin verb, so do not link the two by spelling.
normal.cn: spontaneous 与它拼写相近但来自另一个拉丁动词，不要凭拼写把两者挂钩。

abstract.en: Picture logos lined up on the arch above a marathon start line.
abstract.cn: 想象马拉松起点拱门上排着一行企业标识。

abstract.en: Imagine a contract where money flows one way and publicity the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一份合同：钱流向一方，宣传流向另一方。

abstract.en: Think of a godparent standing beside a child in church.
abstract.cn: 想象教堂里一位教父母站在孩子身旁。

examples.en: The club lost its main sponsorship last season.
examples.cn: 这家俱乐部上赛季失去了主要赞助。

examples.en: Both companies agreed to a three-year sponsorship.
examples.cn: 两家公司达成了一份为期三年的赞助协议。

examples.en: Through the sponsorship of a local charity, the library stayed open.
examples.cn: 在一家本地慈善机构的资助下，图书馆得以继续开放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「四胖的烧鸡」：公司掏钱给活动办酒席，招牌上一排名字，就是 sponsorship 赞助。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 spondere（郑重承诺）→ sponsor（作保者、赞助者）+ 英语后缀 -ship（身份、状况）→ sponsorship，核心义「正式承诺给予的支持」。

sensesIntro.en: Sponsorship grows from one promise of support: the money first, then the written deal, the sponsor role in law, and long-term backing of people.
sensesIntro.cn: sponsorship 从同一个「支持之承诺」长出：先是那笔钱，再是书面协议，然后是法律提案的发起人身份，最后是对个人的长期资助。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: names of backers printed on the board around an event.
core.cn: 核心意象：活动四周的背景板上并排印着赞助者的名字。

branches.en: The money itself is the most common sense.
branches.cn: 那笔资金本身是最常见的义项。

branches.en: The written contract names the arrangement rather than the cash.
branches.cn: 书面合同指向安排本身，而非现金。

branches.en: The role sense keeps the old legal idea of answering for something.
branches.cn: 身份义项保留了替人作保的古老法律意味。

branches.en: Support of people continues the same promise beyond events.
branches.cn: 对个人的资助把同一承诺延续到活动之外。

branches.en: All three are support moving from a backer to a receiver.
branches.cn: 三者都是从赞助者流向受助者的支持。

intro.en: Sponsorship is sponsor plus -ship; English also builds sponsored and sponsorial around the same base.
intro.cn: sponsorship 由 sponsor 加 -ship 构成；英语还围绕同一个基础词构成 sponsored 与 sponsorial。

latinIntro.en: Latin spondere, to promise solemnly, and its family spondeo, sponsus, and sponsio supply the core idea of a binding pledge.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spondere（郑重承诺）及其同族词 spondeo、sponsus、sponsio 提供了「有约束力的承诺」这一核心概念。

items.example: Spondere is the deep Latin root of the family.
items.exampleCN: spondere 是这一词族的深层拉丁词根。

items.meaningCN: 被许诺的人；受承诺约束者
items.example: Sponsus refers to one who has been pledged.
items.exampleCN: sponsus 指被许诺的一方。

items.meaning: a person who gives a pledge
items.example: Sponsor named the pledge giver in Latin.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 sponsor 指作出承诺的人。

items.example: Sponsio is the act of promising.
items.exampleCN: sponsio 指承诺这一行为。

items.meaning: a person or firm that pays for an event
items.meaningCN: 为活动出资的人或公司
items.example: The sponsor paid for the team shirts.
items.exampleCN: 赞助商支付了队服费用。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态、身份或活动的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ship forms sponsorship.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ship 构成 sponsorship。

items.meaning: the act or money of sponsoring
items.example: Sponsorship covered half the costs.
items.exampleCN: 赞助承担了一半费用。

items.meaning: to pay for or back an event
items.example: Banks often sponsor local races.
items.exampleCN: 银行常赞助本地赛事。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms sponsored.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 sponsored。

items.example: He rode in a sponsored cycle race.
items.exampleCN: 他参加了一场有赞助的自行车赛。

definition_zh: 自发的；一时起意的；自然的；非外界强制的
definition_en: happening naturally because of a person own feelings or because of natural causes, not planned or forced
core_image: 水壶盖被蒸汽顶开，自己冒起热水汽
scene: 讲座结束时，全场突然站起鼓掌，没有人事先安排。When the talk ended, the audience stood up and gave spontaneous applause.
sceneCN: 这里 spontaneous 是「自发的、不由安排的」（第 2 个义项：无人组织却自然做出）；句意：讲座结束时，全场自发起身鼓掌。

pos.zh: 非外界强制的；自然发生的

derivatives.zh: 由 spontaneous 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「自发地、不假思索地」
由 spontaneous 的名词形式构成，义为「自发性、自然」
由 spontaneous 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「自发性」

senses.title: Acting from inner impulse
senses.titleCN: 自发行动；不假思索地做
senses.definition: done naturally from a person own wish or feeling, without outside prompting
senses.definitionCN: 出于自己的意愿或感受而自然做出，没有外界推动
senses.example: He gave a spontaneous answer, without thinking first.
senses.exampleCN: 他不假思索地给出了回答。
senses.why: The Latin source is sponte, will or free choice, so a spontaneous act is one that comes from one own will.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sponte 意为「意愿、自由选择」，所以 spontaneous 的行为出于自己的意愿。

senses.title: Happening without planning
senses.titleCN: 无人安排的；自然出现的
senses.definition: happening in a group without being planned or organised beforehand
senses.definitionCN: 在群体中发生，事先未经计划或组织
senses.example: The spontaneous applause surprised the speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 自发的掌声让演讲者很意外。
senses.why: When many people share the same inner impulse at once, the result looks unplanned, which is the group version of the same freedom.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人同时拥有同一种内在冲动，结果看起来就毫无计划，这是同一种自由在群体中的表现。

senses.title: Natural and unrestrained in manner
senses.definition: behaving in a relaxed, natural way that shows genuine feeling and hides nothing
senses.definitionCN: 举止轻松自然，流露真情而不加掩饰
senses.example: Her spontaneous laugh made everyone in the room relax.
senses.exampleCN: 她自然的大笑让屋里的人都放松下来。
senses.why: A manner that rises from inner feeling rather than practice reads as genuine and unforced.
senses.whyCN: 由内心感受而非练习带来的举止，看上去真实而毫不勉强。

senses.title: Arising from natural processes
senses.titleCN: 非外力所致的；自然发生的
senses.definition: developing from natural causes in biology or physics, rather than from an outside hand
senses.definitionCN: 在生物或物理过程中由自然原因产生，而非借助外部力量
senses.example: The bacteria multiply spontaneously under warm conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌在温暖条件下会自行繁殖。
senses.why: The same idea of an inner cause extends from people to natural processes, so the word also means arising without outside agency.
senses.whyCN: 「内在起因」这一想法从人延伸到自然过程，因此这个词也表示无需外部作用而产生。

intro.en: Spontaneous comes from Latin sponte, by free will, with the adjective suffix -aneus, and it entered English through the learned language of the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: spontaneous 来自拉丁语 sponte（出于自愿），带形容词后缀 -aneus，经十七世纪的学术拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The root is usually reconstructed as spe, to flourish or succeed, offered here as a reconstruction.
items.cn: 词根一般认为可重构为 spe，意为繁荣、成功，此处标为重构形式。

items.en: Latins used the adverb sponte, of one own accord, in phrases about free choice.
items.cn: 拉丁人用副词 sponte 表示「出于自己的意愿」，多见于表达自由选择的说法。

items.en: The adjective spontaneus grew from sponte, and meant acting of one own will.
items.cn: 形容词 spontaneus 由 sponte 派生，意为出于自身意愿而行动。

items.en: Spontaneous also came to describe things that happen by their own nature, without human action.
items.cn: 后来 spontaneus 也用来描述依其本性、无需人为作用而发生的事物。

items.en: Spontaneous entered learned English and was soon used in philosophy and science.
items.cn: spontaneous 进入学术英语，随后迅速用于哲学与科学写作。

items.en: Modern English extends it to spontaneous combustion and to everyday unplanned decisions.
items.cn: 现代英语用它描述自燃，也描述日常一时起意的决定。

note.en: Spontaneous belongs to the spontaneous family and stands between natural, unplanned, and unforced words.
note.cn: spontaneous 属于 spontaneous 词族，语义上位于自然、未经计划和未经强制这几类词之间。

entries.definition: in a natural and unplanned way
the quality of being spontaneous
the state of being spontaneous
done without any preparation
acting suddenly on a feeling
entries.definitionCN: 冲动的；凭一时情绪行事的

entries.definition: not arranged in advance

normalIntro.en: Spontaneous starts from sponte, free will: an act, a group reaction, a manner, or a natural process all rise from inside.
normalIntro.cn: spontaneous 从 sponte（自愿）出发：一个行为、一次群体反应、一种举止、一种自然过程，都由内部生发。

normal.en: The Latin adverb sponte, by free will, is the core of spontaneous.
normal.cn: 拉丁语副词 sponte（出于自愿）是 spontaneous 的核心。

normal.en: Spontaneously adds the adverb suffix to the same base.
normal.cn: spontaneously 在同一个词基上加了副词后缀。

normal.en: Spontaneity is the noun, the quality of rising from inner feeling.
normal.cn: spontaneity 是名词，指由内心生发的特质。

normal.en: Spontaneous combustion is chemistry using the same idea: heat rising without a lighter.
normal.cn: spontaneous combustion 是化学上沿用同一个想法：不经点火而自行升温。

normal.en: Compare sponsor: both go back to Latin sp-, but sponsor has spondere, promise, and spontaneous has sponte, will.
normal.cn: 对比 sponsor：两者都以拉丁语 sp- 开头，但 sponsor 有 spondere（承诺），spontaneous 有 sponte（意愿）。

abstract.en: Think of a small plan forming in your mind and your feet already walking.
abstract.cn: 想象心里刚冒出一个念头，脚已经先迈出去了。

abstract.en: Picture a hall where every hand claps at the same instant.
abstract.cn: 想象礼堂里所有人的掌声在同一瞬间响起。

abstract.en: Think of a laugh that bursts out before you can stop it.
abstract.cn: 想象一声大笑在你来得及阻止之前就脱口而出。

examples.en: Their decision to drive to the coast was completely spontaneous.
examples.cn: 他们开车去海边的决定完全是临时起意。

examples.en: The spontaneous applause lasted for several minutes.
examples.cn: 自发的掌声持续了好几分钟。

examples.en: Dry grass can burn spontaneously in hot weather.
examples.cn: 干草在炎热天气里可能自燃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「似喷」：水汽自己往外喷，没人按开关，就是自发的。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sponte（出于自愿）→ 形容词 spontaneus（出于本意、自行发生的）→ 英语 spontaneous，核心义「由内而生、不受外力推动」。

sensesIntro.en: Spontaneous begins with an inner wish, passes to unplanned group actions, then to natural manner, and finally to natural processes with no outside hand.
sensesIntro.cn: spontaneous 先指内在意愿，再指无人组织的群体行为，然后是自然的举止，最后指不借助外力的自然过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steam lifting a lid by its own heat.
core.cn: 核心意象：蒸汽靠着自身的热量把壶盖顶起。

branches.en: Acting from an inner impulse is the closest sense to the Latin root.
branches.cn: 出于内在冲动的行为最贴近拉丁词根。

branches.en: Unplanned group action is the most visible sense in public life.
branches.cn: 未经组织的群体行为是公共生活中最常见的义项。

branches.en: A natural manner turns the inner freedom into visible style.
branches.cn: 自然的举止把内在的自由变成可见的风格。

branches.en: Natural processes repeat the same idea without any actor.
branches.cn: 自然过程把同一想法用在没有任何行动者的情况上。

branches.en: All the human senses share a cause that lies inside the person.
branches.cn: 三个关于人的义项都有共同的起因：原因在人的内部。

intro.en: Spontaneous is a Latin-derived adjective, with the adverb spontaneously and the nouns spontaneity and spontaneousness built from it.
intro.cn: spontaneous 是源自拉丁语的形容词，英语围绕它构成副词 spontaneously 与名词 spontaneity、spontaneousness。

latinIntro.en: Latin sponte, by free will, supplies the stem, and the adjective suffix -aneus shaped spontaneus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sponte（出于自愿）提供词干，形容词后缀 -aneus 构成了 spontaneus。

items.example: Sponte names the free will behind the word.
items.exampleCN: sponte 道出这个词背后的自由意愿。

items.meaningCN: 属于、来自……的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -aneus builds spontaneus.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -aneus 构成 spontaneus。

items.example: Spontaneus described an act of free will.
items.exampleCN: spontaneus 描述出于自由意愿的行为。

items.example: Spontaneous was borrowed into learned English.
items.exampleCN: spontaneous 被借入学术英语。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms spontaneously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 spontaneously。

items.example: The crowd cheered spontaneously.
items.exampleCN: 人群自发地欢呼起来。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms spontaneity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 spontaneity。

items.example: Actors train for spontaneity on stage.
items.exampleCN: 演员训练在舞台上的自然自发性。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms spontaneousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 spontaneousness。

items.meaningCN: 具有……本性的形容词词尾
items.example: The ending -eous keeps the Latin adjective shape.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -eous 保留了拉丁形容词的形态。

definition_zh: 零星的；零散的；不定时发生的；偶发的
definition_en: happening only occasionally or in a few places, rather than regularly or in a continuous way
core_image: 草原上东一团西一团的草，雨云只把雨泼在几块地方
scene: 雨云散去，只留下东一块西一块的湿土和零星的草团。After the clouds broke, only sporadic showers fell on the plain.
sceneCN: 这里 sporadic 是「零星的、不定时发生的」（第 2 个义项：次数与间隔都不固定）；句意：云层散开后，平原上只下了零星的阵雨。

derivatives.zh: 零星地；偶发地，由形容词加 -ally 构成
零星性；偶发性，由形容词加 -ness 构成，较少用
散发病，医学中指偶发而不成规模的病例

senses.title: Scattered in small separate groups
senses.definition: existing or found in a few separate places rather than everywhere
senses.definitionCN: 只在少数彼此分开的地方存在，而不是到处都有
senses.example: Sporadic colonies of plants grow on the rocky slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 岩坡上长着零散的植物群落。
senses.why: The Greek word for scattered seeds paints a literal picture: a few grains sown here and there, not a dense field.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原意是「散播的种子」，画面很具体：只在几处撒下几粒，而不是长成一片密田。

senses.title: Happening at irregular intervals
senses.definition: occurring occasionally and without a regular pattern
senses.definitionCN: 偶尔发生且没有规律
senses.example: The village still hears sporadic gunfire at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里村子里仍听得到零星的枪声。
senses.why: Once the word moved from seeds to events, the idea of scattered in place turned into scattered in time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从种子转向事件后，空间上的「分散」就延伸成了时间上的「间隔不定」。

senses.title: Intermittent in effect
senses.definition: not continuous, so that activity stops and starts again
senses.definitionCN: 不连续，活动会中断又重新开始
senses.example: The radio gave sporadic reports from the flooded area.
senses.exampleCN: 电台从受淹地区发来断断续续的报道。
senses.why: Because the events fall at scattered moments, any output built from them looks broken and uneven.
senses.whyCN: 既然事件零散地落下，由它们构成的结果自然就是断断续续、起伏不定的。

senses.title: Not part of a steady trend
senses.definition: appearing as isolated instances rather than part of a planned or growing process
senses.definitionCN: 表现为孤立个案，而不是计划中或不断增长的过程
senses.example: Their efforts at reform were sporadic and badly coordinated.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的改革努力零敲碎打，协调很差。
senses.why: The Scatter image also evaluates efforts: something sporadic hints at no sustained plan behind it.
senses.whyCN: 「散布」的画面也带有评价色彩：零星的行动背后往往没有持续的规划。

senses.title: Scattered in medicine
senses.definition: of a disease, occurring as separate cases without an epidemic pattern
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病以孤立病例出现，而非流行暴发
senses.example: Doctors reported a few sporadic cases of the infection.
senses.exampleCN: 医生报告了少数散发病例。
senses.why: Medical use keeps the original scattered sense: cases pop up singly, unconnected, like stray seeds.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法保留最初的「分散」义：病例一个个孤立冒出、彼此不相连，就像散落的种子。

intro.en: Sporadic comes from the Greek word for sown, sperien, through the adjective sporadikos, which described seeds scattered here and there; English took it in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: sporadic 来自希腊语 sperien（播种）经过形容词 sporadikos，原指「散播各处的」种子；英语在十七世纪借入。

items.en: Speirein means to sow or scatter seed.
items.cn: speirein 意为播种、撒种。

items.en: Sporas means scattered or dispersed.
items.cn: sporas 意为散落的、分散的。

items.en: Sporadikos describes things found scattered here and there, especially islands.
items.cn: sporadikos 描述零散分布的事物，尤其指岛屿。

items.en: Sporadicus enters scholarly Latin with the same scattered sense.
items.cn: sporadicus 以「零散」义进入学术拉丁语。

items.en: English adopts sporadic, at first mainly in descriptions of scattered plants or cases.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 sporadic，起初多用于描述分散的植物或病例。

items.en: Sporadic widens to events in time: sporadic fighting, sporadic rain.
items.cn: 现代英语中 sporadic 扩展到时间上的事件：零星战斗、零星降雨。

note.en: Sporadic is close to its adverb sporadically and the Greek seed root, and stands near intermittent and occasional words.
note.cn: sporadic 与副词 sporadically、希腊语「种子」词根相邻，在意义上靠近平等的「间歇」「偶尔」类词。

entries.definition: in a scattered or irregular way
the quality of being sporadic
a spore, from the same Greek seed word
entries.definitionCN: 孢子，源自同一个希腊语「种子」词

entries.definition: stopping and starting again at intervals
happening sometimes but not often
single and separate from others

normalIntro.en: Sporadic carries the Greek seed: a handful of grains scattered on the ground, not a whole field.
normalIntro.cn: sporadic 带着希腊语「种子」的画面：地上只撒了几粒，而不是一整片田。

normal.en: Sporadic shares its core with the Greek verb for sowing, so think of seeds scattered in a few spots.
normal.cn: sporadic 与希腊语表示「播种」的动词同源，可想象种子只撒在几处。

normal.en: Sporadic fighting means shelling comes now and then, not every hour.
normal.cn: sporadic fighting 指炮火时有时无，不是整点不停。

normal.en: Sporadic cases in medicine are single cases, not a cluster.
normal.cn: 医学里的 sporadic cases 是个别病例，而不是成群出现。

normal.en: The adverb sporadically tells how rarely or unevenly something happens.
normal.cn: 副词 sporadically 说明某事发生得多么稀少、多么不均匀。

normal.en: Compare intermittent: intermittent stresses stopping and starting, sporadic stresses being scattered and irregular.
normal.cn: 对比 intermittent：intermittent 强调停停走走，sporadic 强调零散、无规律。

abstract.en: Picture a rain cloud that drops water only on three patches of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵雨云只在三块草地上浇水。

abstract.en: Hear a few distant shots at night, separated by long silence.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里偶尔几声远处的枪响，中间隔着长久的寂静。

abstract.en: See a broken radio crackling in now and then with a few words.
abstract.cn: 想象一台坏掉的收音机时有时无地冒出几个字。

examples.en: The region has seen sporadic outbreaks of the disease since spring.
examples.cn: 自春天以来，该地区出现过零星的疾病暴发。

examples.en: Rebel activity in the mountains remained sporadic and unorganised.
examples.cn: 山区的叛乱活动一直是零散而无组织的。

examples.en: Internet service in the village is still poor and only sporadically available.
examples.cn: 村里的网络仍然很差，只是偶尔才有。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死跑让迪克」——迪克跑两步就停下歇歇，零零散散地跑，正好是「零星的、断断续续的」样子；这只是谐音联想，与希腊语词源无关。

root: 希腊语 sperien（播种；撒种）→ sporas（散落的）→ 希腊语 sporadikos（零散分布的）→ 学术拉丁语 sporadicus → 英语 sporadic，核心义「像种子那样散落、零星」。

sensesIntro.en: Sporadic starts with things scattered in space, then moves to events scattered in time, to broken output, to uncoordinated effort, and to isolated medical cases.
sensesIntro.cn: sporadic 先指空间上零散分布的事物，再指时间上零散发生的事件，接着引申为断断续续的输出、不成体系的行为，以及医学上的散发病例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few seeds sown here and there on bare ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：空地上只东一处西一处撒下几粒种子。

branches.en: Scattered in space keeps the literal seed picture.
branches.cn: 空间上的分散保留了种子散落的字面画面。

branches.en: Events falling at scattered moments give the everyday time sense.
branches.cn: 事件在零散时刻出现，就是最日常的时间义。

branches.en: Sporadic events make an output that stops and starts.
branches.cn: 事件零散，造成的结果就断断续续。

branches.en: Scattered presence also reads as lack of a steady plan.
branches.cn: 零散地出现，也读作缺少稳定的计划。

branches.en: A disease pattern follows the same scattered image: single cases, no cluster.
branches.cn: 疾病的分布也沿用散布画面：单个病例，不成群。

intro.en: Sporadic is built on the Greek root spor-, meaning seed or sowing, with the adjective ending -ic and the adverb ending -ally around it.
intro.cn: sporadic 建立在希腊语词根 spor-（种子、播种）之上，围绕它还有形容词词尾 -ic 和副词词尾 -ally。

latinIntro.en: The path runs from Greek speirein to sporas and sporadikos, then through Latin sporadicus into English.
latinIntro.cn: 这条路径从希腊语 speirein 到 sporas、sporadikos，再经拉丁语 sporadicus 进入英语。

items.example: The root spor- gives the seeds image.
items.exampleCN: 词根 spor- 提供种子的画面。

items.example: Speirein means to scatter seed.
items.exampleCN: speirein 意为撒种。

items.example: Sporas names the act of scattering.
items.exampleCN: sporas 指撒播这一动作。

items.example: Sporadikos described scattered islands.
items.exampleCN: sporadikos 原用于描述零散的岛屿。

items.example: Latin sporadicus carries the sense into scholarship.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 sporadicus 把这一含义带入学术用语。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns the root into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 把词根变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ally forms sporadically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成 sporadically。

items.meaningCN: 状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms sporadicness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 sporadicness。

items.example: Sporadically is the common adverb.
items.exampleCN: sporadically 是常用副词。

items.example: Spora keeps the seed sense in biology.
items.exampleCN: spora 在生物学中保留「种子」义。

definition_zh: 零星地；偶尔地；断断续续地；不规则地
definition_en: in a way that happens only occasionally, at irregular intervals, or in a few separate places
core_image: 远处偶尔传来一声枪响，中间隔着一大片寂静
scene: 工地的机器声停了又响，隔很久才又响起一阵。The machinery on the site started up sporadically, then went quiet again.
sceneCN: 这里 sporadically 是「断断续续地、偶尔地」（第 2 个义项：动作停停走走）；句意：工地上的机器断断续续地开动，随后又安静下来。

forms.label: 原形（无比较级与复数变化）

derivatives.zh: 零星的；偶发的，副词去掉 -ly 得到形容词
零星性；偶发性，少见
零星的，罕见的旧式形容词变体

senses.title: Occasionally, not often
senses.definition: in a way that happens from time to time but seldom
senses.definitionCN: 时不时发生但很少发生的方式
senses.example: He jogs sporadically, mostly when the weather is fine.
senses.exampleCN: 他偶尔慢跑，多半是在天气好的时候。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the adjective seed image: actions fall like scattered grains, few and far between.
senses.whyCN: 副词保留了形容词的「种子」画面：动作像散落的谷粒，稀疏、间隔很大。

senses.title: At uneven intervals
senses.definition: with long or unequal gaps between occurrences
senses.definitionCN: 发生之间的间隔很长或不均等
senses.example: Gunfire could be heard sporadically through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里枪声断断续续地传来。
senses.why: Scattered in time becomes a steady stop-and-go rhythm, which English marks with the adverb rather than the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 时间上的「分散」变成了停停走走的节奏，英语习惯用副词而不是形容词来表达这种节奏。

senses.title: In a few separate places
senses.definition: scattered over a wide area in small separate patches
senses.definitionCN: 以小而独立的分布散落在广大区域内
senses.example: Farms are sporadically scattered across the dry valley.
senses.exampleCN: 农庄零散地散布在干旱的山谷里。
senses.why: The place sense survives in the adverb when a verb of position carries it.
senses.whyCN: 当动词表示位置时，空间上的「散布」义就由副词承担下来。

senses.title: Without a regular habit
senses.titleCN: 不经常地；三天打鱼两天晒网地
senses.definition: of a repeated action, done without steady commitment or schedule
senses.definitionCN: 指反复的行为没有稳定的坚持或安排
senses.example: She studied only sporadically and failed the test.
senses.exampleCN: 她学习只是三天打鱼两天晒网，结果没通过考试。
senses.why: Because the occurrences are scattered rather than planned, the adverb can imply an unreliable effort.
senses.whyCN: 发生次数零散而非有规划，所以副词可以暗示努力不可靠。

senses.title: In isolated technical cases
senses.definition: in technical writing, of data or cases that appear singly instead of in a trend
senses.definitionCN: 技术写作中，指数据或病例孤立出现而不成趋势
senses.example: The disease has been reported sporadically in rural counties.
senses.exampleCN: 该病在农村县区零星有报告。
senses.why: Technical use keeps the literal sense of single scattered units, seen in statistics or case reports.
senses.whyCN: 技术用法保留「孤立零星单元」的字面义，见于统计和病例报告。

intro.en: Sporadically is the English adverb of sporadic, built from the Greek seed root spor- plus the Latin adjective ending and the adverbial -ly.
intro.cn: sporadically 是 sporadic 的英语副词，由希腊语「种子」词根 spor- 加拉丁语形容词词尾，再加副词词尾 -ly 构成。

items.en: Speirein means to sow; sporas means a scattering.
items.cn: speirein 意为播种，sporas 意为散布。

items.en: Sporadikos describes things found here and there.
items.cn: sporadikos 指零散分布的事物。

items.en: Sporadicus brings the word into Latin scholarship.
items.cn: sporadicus 把该词带入拉丁语学术圈。

items.en: English borrows sporadic for scattered plants and cases.
items.cn: 英语借入 sporadic，用于分散的植物和病例。

items.en: The adverb sporadically spreads through reports and prose.
items.cn: 副词 sporadically 在报道和散文中流行开来。

items.en: Sporadically now sits beside words like training, service, and outbreaks.
items.cn: 今天 sporadically 常与训练、服务、暴发等词搭配。

note.en: Sporadically is the adverb of sporadic; near it stand intermittent time words and the Greek seed root.
note.cn: sporadically 是 sporadic 的副词；附近有表示间歇的时间词和希腊语「种子」词根。

entries.definition: scattered or irregular
sporadic, now rare
a spore, from the Greek seed word
entries.definitionCN: 孢子，源自同一希腊语「种子」词

entries.definition: with pauses between periods
sometimes but not often
from time to time

normalIntro.en: Sporadically is sporadic with an -ly tail: the seeds are scattered, so the action happens only here and there.
normalIntro.cn: sporadically 就是加 -ly 的 sporadic：种子散落着，所以动作只零散地发生。

normal.en: Pair it with verbs of occurrence: occur, appear, happen sporadically.
normal.cn: 与表示「发生」的动词搭配：occur、appear、happen sporadically。

normal.en: Sporadically available means the service keeps vanishing and returning.
normal.cn: sporadically available 指服务时有时无。

normal.en: The adverb is often used to criticise an effort: he attended only sporadically.
normal.cn: 副词常用来评价不认真的行为：他只是零星地到场。

normal.en: Compare intermittently: both suggest gaps, but sporadically suggests gaps of no fixed size.
normal.cn: 对比 intermittently：两者都指有间隙，但 sporadically 的间隔大小不定。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with spectacularly, which means impressively.
normal.cn: 不要与 spectacularly 混淆，后者意为「壮观地」。

abstract.en: Picture a lighthouse beam sweeping the dark every few minutes.
abstract.cn: 想象灯塔的光每隔几分钟才扫过黑暗一次。

abstract.en: Hear a few scattered clicks on a broken keyboard.
abstract.cn: 想象坏掉的键盘只零星地咔嗒几声。

abstract.en: See a field where crops grow in three lonely patches.
abstract.cn: 想象田里只有三块孤零零的庄稼。

examples.en: The village school is open only sporadically during term time.
examples.cn: 这所村校在学期中只是零星开课。

examples.en: He checked his email sporadically while travelling.
examples.cn: 旅行期间他只是偶尔查看邮件。

examples.en: Rain fell sporadically across the region.
examples.cn: 雨零星地落在整个地区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「四波罗的克利」——四个波罗的海岛屿零星地散在海面上，一会儿看见一个一会儿看不见；这只是谐音联想，与希腊语词源无关。

root: 希腊语 sperien（播种）→ sporadikos（零散分布的）→ 拉丁语 sporadicus → 英语 sporadical → 加副词词尾 -ly 得 sporadically，核心义「像散落的种子那样零星地」。

sensesIntro.en: Sporadically moves from a simple frequency sense to uneven timing, to scattered location, to unreliable habit, and finally to isolated technical cases.
sensesIntro.cn: sporadically 从单纯的频率义开始，转向间隔不均，再到空间分散、习惯不佳，最后落到技术叙述中的孤立个案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single gunshot now and then across a silent field.
core.cn: 核心意象：寂静的旷野上偶尔传来一声枪响。

branches.en: The basic frequency sense is simply seldom.
branches.cn: 基本频率义就是「很少」。

branches.en: Uneven timing adds the feel of long pauses.
branches.cn: 间隔不均义加上长时间停顿的感觉。

branches.en: Place sense keeps the literal scattered seeds.
branches.cn: 位置义保留字面上散落的种子。

branches.en: Rare and unplanned meetings form the unreliable habit sense.
branches.cn: 稀少且无计划的参与构成习惯不佳的意思。

branches.en: Irregular gaps also describe data and cases in reports.
branches.cn: 不规则的间隔也用来描述报告中的数据和病例。

intro.en: Sporadically ends in the common adverb suffix -ly, which sits on the adjective sporadical, built from the Greek root spor-.
intro.cn: sporadically 以常见的副词词尾 -ly 结尾，其下是形容词 sporadical，词根来自希腊语 spor-。

latinIntro.en: Latin sporadicus supplies the adjective, and English adds -al and -ly to build the adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sporadicus 提供形容词，英语再加 -al 与 -ly 构成副词。

items.example: The root spor- keeps the seed image.
items.exampleCN: 词根 spor- 保留种子画面。

items.example: Sporas means a scattering of seed.
items.exampleCN: sporas 意为撒播种子。

items.example: Sporadikos names scattered things.
items.exampleCN: sporadikos 指零散的事物。

items.example: Sporadicus passes into European usage.
items.exampleCN: sporadicus 进入欧洲语言的用法。

items.example: The suffix -al forms sporadical.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 sporadical。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms sporadic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成 sporadic。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms sporadically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 sporadically。

items.meaningCN: 状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms sporadicness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 sporadicness。

items.example: Sporadic is the adjective behind the adverb.
items.exampleCN: sporadic 是副词背后的形容词。

definition_zh: 配偶；丈夫或妻子
definition_en: a husband or wife, especially one seen from the point of view of the other partner, often in formal or legal contexts
core_image: 婚礼上面对面交换戒指的两个人，彼此互为「另一半」
scene: 移民表格上有一栏，要求申请人写清伴侣的关系与身份。Applicants must list their spouse on the immigration form.
sceneCN: 这里 spouse 是「配偶」（第 1 个义项：法律或正式语境中的丈夫或妻子）；句意：申请人必须在移民表格上填明配偶。

derivatives.zh: 配偶的；婚姻的，由 spouse 加 -al 构成
无配偶的，较少用
与「订约、许诺」词根相关，意为订婚，此处只作同源联想

senses.title: A husband or wife in formal contexts
senses.definition: the person someone is married to, named as a legal or official category
senses.definitionCN: 某人结婚的对象，作为法律或正式的类别来称呼
senses.example: The form asks whether your spouse is employed.
senses.exampleCN: 表格要求填写你的配偶是否有工作。
senses.why: The core image is the vow itself: the person you had promised yourself to becomes your spouse.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象就是那场婚誓：被你许诺要与之共同生活的人，就成了你的配偶。

senses.title: The other member of a married pair
senses.definition: either of the two married people, seen from the point of view of the other
senses.definitionCN: 婚姻中的两个人之一，从另一方的角度看
senses.example: Employees may bring their spouses to the annual dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 员工可以带伴侣参加年度晚宴。
senses.why: Said from the inside, the word avoids choosing husband or wife and simply names the counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 从当事人角度说，这个词避开「丈夫」还是「妻子」的选择，直接指称对方那一方。

senses.title: Partner in a legal relationship
senses.definition: a legally recognised partner under marriage or civil union law
senses.definitionCN: 依婚姻法或民事伴侣法得到法律承认的伴侣
senses.example: The pension passes to the spouse of the deceased.
senses.exampleCN: 抚恤金转给已故者的配偶。
senses.why: Law keeps spouse neutral so rights apply to any legally married partner, whatever the gender.
senses.whyCN: 法律让 spouse 保持中性，所以无论性别，只要是合法婚姻对象，权利都同样适用。

senses.title: A spouse in tax and benefit rules
senses.definition: the partner whose income or status counts for tax, benefits, or allowances
senses.definitionCN: 其收入或身份会影响税务、福利或津贴的伴侣
senses.example: Couples can transfer some allowance to a spouse.
senses.exampleCN: 夫妻可以把部分免税额转给配偶。
senses.why: Administrative rules need a fixed category, so the formal spouse sense turns into a tax label.
senses.whyCN: 行政规则需要固定的类别，于是正式的配偶义变成了税务标签。

senses.title: The marriage partner in everyday speech
senses.titleCN: （口语中代替 husband 或 wife）
senses.definition: an alternative to husband or wife, sometimes used to stay neutral or discreet
senses.definitionCN: 作为丈夫或妻子的替代说法，有时为中性或不点名而用
senses.example: She introduced her spouse to the new neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 她把配偶介绍给新邻居。
senses.why: Spoken English borrows the neutral legal word to avoid revealing gender or to sound formal.
senses.whyCN: 口语借用这个中性的法律词，以不透露性别或显得正式。

intro.en: Spouse comes from Latin sponsus and sponsa, meaning a betrothed or promised person, from spondere, to promise solemnly; Old French espous brought it into English.
intro.cn: spouse 来自拉丁语 sponsus 与 sponsa（订婚者、被许诺的人），源于动词 spondere（庄严许诺）；经古法语 espous 进入英语。

items.en: Spondere means to promise solemnly, especially in a betrothal.
items.cn: spondere 意为庄严许诺，尤指订婚时的承诺。

items.en: Sponsus and sponsa name the betrothed man and woman.
items.cn: sponsus 与 sponsa 分别指订婚的男子与女子。

items.en: Espous means a wedding or a spouse.
items.cn: espous 意为婚礼或配偶。

items.en: Spouse enters English as a general word for a married partner.
items.cn: spouse 进入中古英语，泛指已婚的伴侣。

items.en: Husband and wife take over everyday speech, leaving spouse formal.
items.cn: husband 与 wife 占据日常口语，spouse 退向正式语域。

items.en: Modern use makes spouse a neutral legal and administrative term.
items.cn: 现代用法使 spouse 成为中性的法律与行政用语。

note.en: Spouse is the formal, neutral word for a married partner; around it sit its adjective spousal and the older promise root, then the familiar husband and wife words.
note.cn: spouse 是表示「已婚伴侣」的正式中性词；它周围有形容词 spousal 和古老的「许诺」词根，再往外是常见的 husband、wife 等词。

entries.definition: relating to a spouse or marriage
to adopt a cause as your own, once meaning to marry
entries.definitionCN: 拥护；支持（旧义为娶、嫁），同源于许诺

entries.definition: an answer, literally a promise back
entries.definitionCN: 回答；回应，字面义为「反向许诺」，同源但意义已远

entries.definition: a married man, seen from his partner side
a married woman, seen from her partner side
the person someone lives with or is committed to
entries.definitionCN: 伴侣，不只限于婚姻关系

normalIntro.en: Spouse began as a promise: the spondere root means to pledge, and the person you pledged to is your spouse.
normalIntro.cn: spouse 最初来自「许诺」：词根 spondere 意为郑重承诺，被你许诺的人就是你的配偶。

normal.en: The -ous in spouse hints at spouse and spousal sharing a family: both mean of a married partner.
normal.cn: spouse 与 spousal 同族，后者直接表示「配偶的、婚姻的」。

normal.en: Tax and visa forms use spouse because it covers both husband and wife.
normal.cn: 税表和签证表用 spouse，因为它同时包括丈夫和妻子。

normal.en: Mind the spelling: spouse has a soft s, and the letter is not a z sound. This spelling trap belongs to spouse itself, not to a different word.
normal.cn: 注意拼写与发音：spouse 里的 s 发清音，不像 house 中的浊音。

normal.en: Compare partner, which does not require marriage; spouse does.
normal.cn: 对比 partner：partner 不要求结婚，spouse 则指已婚伴侣。

normal.en: The former spouse is the person you used to be married to.
normal.cn: former spouse 指前夫或前妻。

abstract.en: Picture two hands joined on a marriage certificate.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手握在结婚证书上。

abstract.en: See a form with one box labelled spouse and another labelled children.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，一栏写配偶，一栏写子女。

abstract.en: Think of a shared bank account with one name printed beside the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一个联名账户，一个名字印在另一个名字旁边。

examples.en: She listed her spouse as the main contact on the medical form.
examples.cn: 她在医疗表上填写配偶为主要联系人。

examples.en: Employees can add a spouse to the company health plan.
examples.cn: 员工可以把配偶加入公司医疗保险。

examples.en: The will leaves the house to his spouse and the savings to his children.
examples.cn: 遗嘱把房子留给配偶，存款留给子女。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯宝仕」——身边那个像宝贝一样、被请来一起生活的「是宝」之人，就是配偶；这只是谐音联想，与拉丁语 spondere 的词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 spondere（庄严许诺）→ sponsus、sponsa（订婚者）→ 古法语 espous → 英语 spouse，核心义「与你互相许诺的那一方」。

sensesIntro.en: Spouse begins as an official word for a married partner, then names the other half of a pair, then a legal category, a tax rule, and finally a neutral everyday substitute for husband or wife.
sensesIntro.cn: spouse 先是已婚伴侣的正式称呼，再指一对中的另一方，然后成为法律类别与税务规则用语，最后在日常口语里作为丈夫或妻子的中性替代词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people facing each other, each the other half.
core.cn: 核心意象：面对面站着的两个人，各自都是对方的另一半。

branches.en: The formal sense keeps the official tone of the original promise.
branches.cn: 正式义保留了最初「许诺」的官方口吻。

branches.en: The pair sense names the counterpart from your own side.
branches.cn: 配对义从自己的角度指称对方那一方。

branches.en: Law makes the promise a defined relation with rights.
branches.cn: 法律把许诺变成有权利界定的关系。

branches.en: Forms and rules turn the person into a category on paper.
branches.cn: 表格与规则把这个人变成纸面上的类别。

branches.en: Everyday use borrows the neutral term to avoid saying husband or wife.
branches.cn: 日常用法借用中性词，避免说出丈夫或妻子。

intro.en: Spouse is a bare Latin loanword; its ending -se hides the Latin suffix, and English builds spousal and spouseless on it.
intro.cn: spouse 是完整的拉丁语借词，结尾 -se 背后是拉丁语词尾；英语在它之上构成 spousal 与 spouseless。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb spondere, to promise, gives the noun sponsus and its feminine sponsa, the promised person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 spondere（许诺）派生名词 sponsus 与阴性形式 sponsa，指被许诺的人。

items.example: Spondere is the promise at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: spondere 是这个词核心的「许诺」。

items.example: Sponsus gives the masculine sense.
items.exampleCN: sponsus 提供阳性义。

items.example: Sponsa gives the feminine sense.
items.exampleCN: sponsa 提供阴性义。

items.example: The endings mark the two married roles.
items.exampleCN: 这些词尾区分婚姻中的两种角色。

items.example: Espous carries the word into French.
items.exampleCN: espous 把这个词带入法语。

items.example: The suffix -al forms spousal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 spousal。

items.example: The suffix -less forms spouseless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 spouseless。

items.example: Spousal is the everyday relative.
items.exampleCN: spousal 是它的常用形容词。

items.example: Espouse keeps the promise sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: espouse 保留词根的「许诺」义。

definition_zh: 喷口；壶嘴；喷出；滔滔不绝地讲
definition_en: a tube or opening through which liquid flows out in a stream, and to send that liquid out forcefully
core_image: 一只细长的壶嘴，热水从管口猛地冲出来
scene: 雨下得太急，老屋檐下的铁管倒成了排水渠，水顺着断开的管口往外喷。The broken pipe under the roof spouted water all over the courtyard.
sceneCN: 这里 spout 是「喷出」（第 3 个义项：液体从管口猛烈流出）；句意：屋顶下断裂的管子往院子里到处喷水。

pos.zh: 喷出；喷涌；滔滔不绝地讲

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -er 构成，指爱滔滔不绝讲话的人或会喷水的物体
由名词加 -less 构成，义为没有壶嘴或喷口的
水与喷口复合，义为海龙卷或排水管

senses.title: A tube or opening that pours
senses.definition: a short tube or narrow opening on a container, through which liquid is poured
senses.definitionCN: 容器上用来倒出液体的短管或窄口
senses.example: Pour the tea slowly from the spout of the pot.
senses.exampleCN: 从茶壶的壶嘴慢慢倒茶。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the tube that pours liquid out, and the image of the narrow opening comes first.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项就是倒出液体的管子，核心意象先是「窄口」这一实物。

senses.title: Water thrown up in a column
senses.definition: a tall jet of water or spray sent up into the air
senses.definitionCN: 向空中喷起高高的水柱或水花
senses.example: A whale blew a tall spout near the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 一头鲸在船边喷起高高的水柱。
senses.why: The opening sends water straight up, so the water column itself takes the name of the tube.
senses.whyCN: 管口把水直直送向空中，于是喷起的水柱本身也沿用了这个词。

senses.title: To send liquid out in a stream
senses.definition: to pour or send liquid out forcefully in a continuous stream
senses.definitionCN: 使液体成股地猛烈流出
senses.example: The broken pipe spouted water all over the courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 断裂的管子往院子里到处喷水。
senses.why: From the noun the verb grows: what the tube does to liquid, the whole pipe now does too.
senses.whyCN: 动词从名词长出：管子对液体做的事，整根管道也这么做。

senses.title: To speak on and on
senses.titleCN: 滔滔不绝地讲；连珠炮似地说
senses.definition: to talk at length, often loudly and in a way that others find tiresome
senses.definitionCN: 长久、常常大声地讲话，往往令旁人厌烦
senses.example: He spouted on about his old job for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他滔滔不绝地讲了一个小时的旧工作。
senses.why: Speech pours out like water from the opening, so long endless talk borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 话像水从管口喷涌而出，于是没完没了的长篇大论借用了这个词。

senses.title: To say things without thinking
senses.definition: to repeat words or opinions mechanically, often without understanding them
senses.definitionCN: 不加思考地照搬重复言语或意见
senses.example: The actor spouted his lines without any feeling.
senses.exampleCN: 那名演员毫无感情地背台词。
senses.why: If words gush out freely and carelessly, they blur into mere noise from the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 如果话只是漫无遮拦地涌出，便成了嘴里的噪音。

senses.title: A pipe or gutter that carries water
senses.definition: a pipe or channel that carries rain water down from a roof
senses.definitionCN: 把雨水从屋顶引下的管子或沟槽
senses.example: Rain raced down the spout beside the door.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水顺着门边的落水管奔流而下。
senses.why: The older sense of a watering channel returns in British building terms for downpipes.
senses.whyCN: 「引水的沟槽」这一旧义在英式建筑用语里回到落水管上。

senses.title: A channel in a pipe for grain or air
senses.definition: a sloping channel through which grain, coal, or air passes in a machine
senses.definitionCN: 机器里让谷物、煤或空气通过的倾斜通道
senses.example: Coal slid down the spout into the wagon.
senses.exampleCN: 煤顺着料槽滑进车厢。
senses.why: The pouring tube is generalized to any channel that lets loose material slide down.
senses.whyCN: 倒水的管子被泛化成了任何让松散物料滑下的通道。

intro.en: Spout is related to the verb spit and probably to spout as a pouring tube, though the exact origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: spout 与 spit（吐、喷）同源的可能性较大，一般认为由「吐出、喷出」的动作引申为「管子」，确切来源存疑。

items.en: A reconstructed root related to sp-out may mean to spit or spurt.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个与「吐、喷」相关的重构词根 sp- 系列，此处存疑。

items.en: Spouten means to spout or spurt out, first recorded around the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语 spouten 意为喷出、涌出，约在十四世纪见于记载。

items.en: The noun spout names a spout or pipe, often a gutter.
items.cn: 中古英语名词 spout 指喷口、管子，多为排水沟槽。

items.en: The word spreads to whales, fountains, and gutters.
items.cn: 早期现代英语里，这个词扩展到鲸、喷泉与排水沟。

items.en: The verb gains the figurative sense of pouring out words.
items.cn: 现代英语里，动词又添上「把话倒出来」的比喻义。

items.en: Spout survives in compounds such as waterspout and teapot spout.
items.cn: 现代英语里，spout 保留在 waterspout、teapot spout 等复合词中。

note.en: Spout belongs to a small family of pouring and spurting words, close to spit and spurt in form and to gush and pour in meaning.
note.cn: spout 属于一小簇表示「喷射、倒出」的词，形式上贴近 spit、spurt，意义上贴近 gush、pour。

entries.definition: to force liquid or food out of the mouth
entries.definitionCN: 吐出；啐；与喷口义可能同源

entries.definition: to shoot out suddenly in a small stream
entries.definitionCN: 喷出；涌出（与 spout 同属喷溅词群）

entries.definition: to begin to grow and put out shoots
entries.definitionCN: 发芽；长出（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to flow out quickly and in large amounts
to make a liquid flow out of a container
to say words in a language
entries.definitionCN: 说；讲（对应滔滔不绝地说的近邻）

normalIntro.en: Spout is a pouring tube first and a gushing action second, so learn it with water images.
normalIntro.cn: spout 先是「倒水的管子」，再是「喷出」的动作，配合水的画面最好记。

normal.en: A spout is the narrow tube on a teapot or watering can.
normal.cn: spout 是茶壶或洒水壶上那根细细的壶嘴。

normal.en: To spout water is to send it out in a strong stream.
normal.cn: to spout water 就是让水成股地猛喷出来。

normal.en: A waterspout is a twisting column of water in the sky or under a drainpipe.
normal.cn: waterspout 是海上的水龙卷，或排水管口下的水柱。

normal.en: To spout nonsense is to talk on without sense.
normal.cn: spout nonsense 就是不住嘴地胡说。

normal.en: Compare spurt: spurt is a short sudden burst, while spout suggests a steady pouring stream.
normal.cn: 对比 spurt：spurt 是短促的一股，spout 更像持续的成股浇流。

abstract.en: Picture the lip of a teapot, thin and round, tipping forward.
abstract.cn: 想象茶壶的壶嘴又细又圆，正向前倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a fountain sending one straight white column upward.
abstract.cn: 想象泉眼向上送出一道笔直的白色水柱。

abstract.en: Picture words pouring from a mouth as if from a pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象话语从嘴里涌出，像从管子里倒出来。

examples.en: Water spouted from a crack in the old pipe.
examples.cn: 水从旧管子的裂缝里喷了出来。

examples.en: She filled the kettle through the spout.
examples.cn: 她顺着壶嘴把水灌进水壶。

examples.en: The guide spouted facts about the castle without stopping.
examples.cn: 导游不停地滔滔不绝讲着城堡的掌故。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死泡噗」——热水灌进去，管口一「噗」地往外喷；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为与 spit（吐、喷）同属一个拟声性的「喷吐」词群，中古英语 spouten（喷出）→ 名词「喷嘴、排水管」→ 动词「喷出、滔滔不绝地说」；确切来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Spout starts as the pouring tube, moves to the water column it throws up, and then to the pouring action it performs, finally reaching the human voice.
sensesIntro.cn: spout 从「倒水的管子」出发，到它喷起的水柱，再到它完成的「喷出」动作，最后落到人嘴上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow spout shooting water straight out.
core.cn: 核心意象：细细的壶嘴把水直直喷出去。

branches.en: The tube itself is the concrete everyday sense.
branches.cn: 管口本身是最具体、最日常的义项。

branches.en: The water it throws up is named after the tube.
branches.cn: 它喷起的水柱沿用了管子的名字。

branches.en: The pouring action is the verb sense.
branches.cn: 喷出的动作是动词义项。

branches.en: Endless talk and thoughtless talk both pour words like water.
branches.cn: 没完没了地讲与不加思考地说，都是把话像水一样倒出来。

branches.en: Gutters and machine channels are extensions of the pouring tube.
branches.cn: 落水管与机器料槽都是倒水管子的延伸。

intro.en: Spout is a short Germanic word with few affixes, but it forms compounds with water and teapot.
intro.cn: spout 是短小的日耳曼源词，词缀很少，但能与水、茶壶等词构成复合。

latinIntro.en: There is no direct Latin ancestor for spout, so the Latin list is short.
latinIntro.cn: spout 没有直接的拉丁祖词，拉丁同源词表因此很短。

items.example: The teapot has a long spout.
items.exampleCN: 这把茶壶壶嘴很长。

items.meaning: a tornado over water or a pipe outlet
items.example: A waterspout formed off the coast.
items.exampleCN: 海岸外形成了一股海龙卷。

items.meaning: a pipe that carries rain down
items.example: The downspout was blocked with leaves.
items.exampleCN: 落水管被树叶堵住了。

items.example: A spoutless jug is hard to pour from.
items.exampleCN: 没有嘴的罐子很难倒水。

items.example: The spouter never stopped for breath.
items.exampleCN: 那个夸夸其谈的人从不歇口气。

items.example: A spouted cup keeps the tea from spilling.
items.exampleCN: 有嘴的杯子能让茶不洒出来。

items.example: The spouting fountain drew a crowd.
items.exampleCN: 喷涌的喷泉吸引了一群人。

items.example: Water shot from the whale spout-hole.
items.exampleCN: 水从鲸的呼吸孔里射出。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 吐出（与 spout 远缘，一般认为同属喷吐词群）
起泡（与喷水意象相近，并非同源）

definition_zh: 伸开四肢坐着或躺着；蔓延；无序扩展；散乱的建筑群
definition_en: to sit or lie with the arms and legs spread out, and to spread out over a wide area in an untidy way
core_image: 一个人摊开手脚躺在沙发上，四肢朝四面八方展开
scene: 周末下午，客厅地板上摊着漫画和零食袋，他整个人张开手脚陷在沙发里，一动不动。The children sprawled on the grass after the long walk.
sceneCN: 这里 sprawl 是「摊开四肢躺下」（第 1 个义项：伸开手脚放松地坐或躺）；句意：走了很久之后，孩子们摊开四肢躺在草地上。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为蔓延的、杂乱延伸的
由动词加 -er 构成，指摊手摊脚的人或蔓延的事物
过去分词用作形容词，义为摊开的、乱伸的

senses.title: To sit or lie with limbs spread out
senses.definition: to sit, lie, or fall with the arms and legs spread out loosely
senses.definitionCN: 松散地张开手臂与双腿坐着、躺着或倒下
senses.example: The children sprawled on the grass after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 走了很久之后，孩子们摊开四肢躺在草地上。
senses.why: The original picture is a body thrown open limb by limb on the ground, slack and relaxed.
senses.whyCN: 最初的画面是一具身体把四肢一股脑朝地面摊开，松散又放松。

senses.title: To spread across a surface untidily
senses.definition: to spread out loosely and without order over an area or surface
senses.definitionCN: 松散无序地铺满一片地方或表面
senses.example: Books and papers sprawled across the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 书和纸乱七八糟摊满了书桌。
senses.why: Things lying loosely, like limbs, spread out far and untidily over a surface.
senses.whyCN: 物件像摊开的四肢一样松散躺着，就在表面上摊得又远又乱。

senses.title: To grow outward in all directions
senses.definition: to grow or extend outward in unruly directions
senses.definitionCN: 不受约束地朝各个方向生长、延伸
senses.example: Wild roses sprawl over the garden wall.
senses.exampleCN: 野蔷薇蔓延在花园的围墙上。
senses.why: A creeping plant does what a sprawled body does: it reaches out on every side.
senses.whyCN: 蔓生植物的行为正如摊开的身体：朝四面八方伸出去。

senses.title: To spread over a wide area of land
senses.definition: to spread over a large area of land, often in an unplanned way
senses.definitionCN: 在广大地域内扩展，往往缺乏规划
senses.example: The town has sprawled along the valley floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇沿着谷底不断无序扩展。
senses.why: When settlements reach out like arms, the word grows from posture to geography.
senses.whyCN: 当聚居地向四方像手臂那样伸出，「姿势」的词义便长到了地理上。

senses.title: An untidy spread of buildings
senses.definition: a wide, untidy area of buildings or settlement
senses.definitionCN: 宽广而杂乱的建筑或聚居区
senses.example: The edge of the city turned into a sprawl of warehouses.
senses.exampleCN: 城市边缘变成了一片散乱的仓库区。
senses.why: The untidy outward spread becomes a noun for the resulting landscape.
senses.whyCN: 那种无序向外铺开的景象，被名词化成了最终形成的景观。

senses.title: Out of control growth of a city
senses.definition: the rapid, unplanned outward growth of a town or city
senses.definitionCN: 城镇快速而无计划的向外扩张
senses.example: Urban sprawl has swallowed most of the farmland.
senses.exampleCN: 城市无序扩张吞掉了大部分农田。
senses.why: Planners turned the image of loose limbs into a critique of cities that grow without shape.
senses.whyCN: 规划者把「松散四肢」的意象变成了对「长而无形的城市」的批评。

senses.title: A loose, awkward way of lying
senses.definition: to fall or lie down heavily and awkwardly
senses.definitionCN: 沉重而笨拙地倒下或躺下
senses.example: He sprawled face down in the doorway.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸朝下狼狈地趴在门口。
senses.why: The core limb image also covers a sudden, heavy fall where the body flops open.
senses.whyCN: 核心的四肢意象也涵盖突然重摔、身体摊开的场面。

intro.en: Sprawl probably comes from Old English sprawlian, to sprawl or kick, of uncertain ultimate origin.
intro.cn: sprawl 一般认为来自古英语 sprawlian（伸腿扑腾），更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Sprawlian means to sprawl or to struggle with the limbs.
items.cn: 古英语 sprawlian 意为摊开四肢或伸腿扑腾。

items.en: Related forms spread in northern and western dialects.
items.cn: 相关词形在中古英语的北部与西部方言中扩散。

items.en: The verb is recorded with the sense of lying with limbs spread out.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，这个动词被记录为「张开四肢躺着」。

items.en: The word begins to describe towns and buildings spreading outwards.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，这个词开始描述城镇与建筑向外铺展。

items.en: Urban sprawl becomes a standard term in planning and geography.
items.cn: 现代英语中，urban sprawl 成为规划与地理学的标准术语。

note.en: Sprawl is a loose spreading word, close to sprinkle and spray in form and to spread and extend in meaning.
note.cn: sprawl 是表示「松散铺开」的词，形式贴近 sprinkle、spray，意义贴近 spread、extend。

entries.definition: a mist of fine drops or to scatter liquid
entries.definitionCN: 水花；喷雾（只是拼写相近，词根不同）

entries.definition: to scatter small drops or pieces
entries.definitionCN: 撒；洒（与 sprawl 形近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to stretch out fully on a surface
to open out or extend over a wider area
to reach or stretch over an area
to reach the limbs out fully

normalIntro.en: Sprawl is the picture of limbs thrown open, so liken it to arms and legs loosening outward.
normalIntro.cn: sprawl 是「四肢摊开」的画面，可以把它记成手脚朝外放松舒展。

normal.en: To sprawl out is to stretch the arms and legs wide on a surface.
normal.cn: to sprawl out 就是在某处把手脚大大摊开。

normal.en: Urban sprawl describes a city creeping untidily outwards.
normal.cn: urban sprawl 描述城市乱糟糟地向外蔓延。

normal.en: A sprawling city never seems to stop growing.
normal.cn: a sprawling city 像是永远停不下生长。

normal.en: Papers sprawled across the desk means they covered it in no order.
normal.cn: papers sprawled across the desk 意思是没有次序地铺满桌面。

normal.en: Compare spread: spread is neutral, while sprawl adds the idea of looseness and disorder.
normal.cn: 对比 spread：spread 中性，sprawl 多了「松散与混乱」的味道。

abstract.en: Picture four limbs opening on a wide carpet.
abstract.cn: 想象四肢在一大片地毯上舒展开来。

abstract.en: Picture a vine creeping over a whole wall.
abstract.cn: 想象藤蔓爬满了整面墙。

abstract.en: Picture a town leaking away from its centre in every direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城镇从中心朝四面八方漫出去。

examples.en: Cats sprawl in the sunshine for hours.
examples.cn: 猫在阳光下摊开身子一躺就是几个小时。

examples.en: The city sprawls for miles along the coast.
examples.cn: 这座城市沿着海岸延伸了好几英里。

examples.en: Critics blame sprawl for the loss of green fields.
examples.cn: 批评者把绿地的流失归咎于城市的无序扩张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死扑挠」——人一摊开四肢就成大字，手里还乱「扑腾乱挠」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 sprawlian（摊开肢体、伸腿扑腾）→ 中古英语方言 → 动词「摊开四肢躺倒」→ 十九世纪起延伸到城镇、建筑「无序向外铺开」；更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Sprawl begins with a relaxed body opening its limbs, spreads to things lying loosely on a surface, and ends with cities growing outward without shape.
sensesIntro.cn: sprawl 从舒展四肢的身体开始，移到表面松散摊开的物件，最后落到长而无形的城市。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body lying with four limbs thrown wide open.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体摊开，四肢大大张开。

branches.en: The relaxed body is the first and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 放松摊开的身体是最直白的义项。

branches.en: Loose things lying on a surface copy the open limbs.
branches.cn: 物件松散地铺满表面，正像张开的四肢。

branches.en: Creeping plants reach out in every direction like those limbs.
branches.cn: 蔓生植物像四肢一样朝四面八方伸展。

branches.en: Settlements reach outward and the result is an untidy landscape.
branches.cn: 聚居地向外伸出，结果就是杂乱的景观。

branches.en: City overflow is the planning sense, and a heavy fall is the last bodily echo.
branches.cn: 城市扩张是规划义，重重摔倒则是身体的最后回声。

intro.en: Sprawl has few affixes of its own, but its -ing and -er forms are common in geography and everyday speech.
intro.cn: sprawl 自身的词缀不多，但它的 -ing、-er 形式在地理与日常表达里很常见。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor; related Latin forms below are merely distant.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁祖词，下面列出的拉丁形式只是远缘。

items.example: They sprawled on the beach.
items.exampleCN: 他们摊开身子躺在海滩上。

items.example: A sprawling suburb grew around the station.
items.exampleCN: 车站四周长出大片杂乱的郊区。

items.example: A map lay sprawled across the table.
items.exampleCN: 一张地图摊在桌上。

items.meaning: one who or that which sprawls
items.example: The dog is a famous sprawler on the rug.
items.exampleCN: 这条狗是出了名爱摊在毯子上。

items.example: He sprawled out in the empty seat.
items.exampleCN: 他在空座位上摊开身子。

items.example: The town passed an anti-sprawl rule.
items.exampleCN: 小镇通过了一条反扩张规定。

items.example: The valley remained largely sprawl-free.
items.exampleCN: 这片山谷大体上没有无序扩张。

items.example: Urban sprawl wastes farmland and fuel.
items.exampleCN: 城市无序扩张浪费农田与燃料。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 撒开；分散（远缘，并非同源）
散开的（与 sprawl 意象相近，来源不同）

definition_zh: 喷雾器；喷洒器；喷药机
definition_en: a device that forces liquid out in fine drops over a surface, used in farming, cleaning, or painting
core_image: 一只手握着喷壶，细密的水雾从瓶口散开落在叶子上
scene: 果园里，果农背着水箱，一手压杆一手举着喷嘴，药雾细细地散落在每片叶子上。The farmer loaded the sprayer and walked down the rows of apple trees.
sceneCN: 这里 sprayer 是「喷雾器、喷洒器」（第 1 个义项：把液体打成细雾喷出去的器具）；句意：农夫装好喷药机，沿着苹果树行走去。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -er 得到的动词与名词，义为喷射、水雾
由动词 spray 加 -ing 构成，义为喷洒作业
由 spray 加 -able 构成，义为可喷洒的
spray 与 man 复合，指喷药工

senses.title: A device that squirts liquid
senses.definition: a device that breaks liquid into fine drops and sends them out over a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把液体打成细雾喷到表面上的器具
senses.example: She filled the garden sprayer with soapy water.
senses.exampleCN: 她把园艺喷壶灌满了肥皂水。
senses.why: The suffix -er makes an agent noun, so a sprayer is simply the thing that sprays.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 构成表示工具的名词，所以 sprayer 就是「会喷的东西」。

senses.title: A machine for farm chemicals
senses.definition: a large machine or tank used to apply pesticides or fertiliser to crops
senses.definitionCN: 给庄稼喷洒农药或肥料的机器或大水箱
senses.example: The sprayer saved the orchard from aphids.
senses.exampleCN: 喷药机保住了果园，免遭蚜虫侵害。
senses.why: Farm work turns the general gizmo into a heavy tank trailed behind a tractor.
senses.whyCN: 农业用途把通用器具变成挂在拖拉机后的重型水箱。

senses.title: A painting or cleaning unit
senses.definition: a device that coats or washes a surface with liquid under pressure
senses.definitionCN: 以压力把液体涂在或洗在表面上的装置
senses.example: He rented a paint sprayer for the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他租了一台喷漆机来刷栅栏。
senses.why: Push the agent noun into trade use and it names paint guns and pressure washers.
senses.whyCN: 把这个工具名词推进行业用语，就指喷漆枪和高压清洗机。

senses.title: The person who operates the device
senses.definition: a worker whose job is to apply sprays to crops or surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 负责给作物或表面喷洒的工人
senses.example: A trained sprayer must wear gloves and a mask.
senses.exampleCN: 受过培训的喷洒工必须戴手套和口罩。
senses.why: Some agent nouns name tools, others name people, and here both readings exist side by side.
senses.whyCN: 有些 -er 名词指工具，有些指人，而这里两种读法并存。

senses.title: A fine mist producer
senses.definition: any small unit that releases a fine mist, such as in cosmetics or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 任何释放细雾的小装置，如化妆品或医疗用
senses.example: The nasal sprayer delivers a measured dose.
senses.exampleCN: 鼻腔喷雾器给出定量的药雾。
senses.why: The core job of the tool, making droplets small, carries into clinics and cosmetics.
senses.whyCN: 这个工具的核心本领是把水滴打细，于是进了诊室与化妆品柜台。

intro.en: Sprayer is spray plus the agent suffix -er, and spray itself is probably from Middle Dutch sprayen, to sprinkle.
intro.cn: sprayer 由 spray 加表示工具或人的后缀 -er 构成；spray 一般认为来自中古荷兰语 sprayen（喷洒）。

items.en: Sprayen means to sprinkle or squirt small drops.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 sprayen 意为洒、溅出小水滴。

items.en: Spray enters English as a verb meaning to sprinkle.
items.cn: 十六世纪 spray 进入英语，作动词意为喷洒。

items.en: The -er agent noun names the tool that breaks liquid into mist.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，-er 工具名词指出把液体打细成雾的器具。

items.en: Sprayer spreads into farming, painting, and household care.
items.cn: 二十世纪起，sprayer 扩展到农业、喷漆与家庭护理。

items.en: Fine nozzle design turns the sprayer into a precise dosing unit.
items.cn: 现代英语里，精细喷嘴设计让喷雾器成了能精准计量的装置。

note.en: Sprayer is the tool made from spray, sitting beside sprinkle and spout in form and next to atomizer and sprinkler in meaning.
note.cn: sprayer 是由 spray 造出的工具名词，形式邻接 sprinkle、spout，意义邻接 atomizer、sprinkler。

entries.definition: to send liquid out in fine drops
a tube that pours liquid out
entries.definitionCN: 喷口；壶嘴（与 spray 形近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a person who lies with limbs spread
entries.definitionCN: 摊开四肢的人（与 sprayer 形近，词根不同）

entries.definition: a device that turns liquid into fine mist
a device that scatters water over a lawn or field
a can that releases liquid as a spray

normalIntro.en: Sprayer is simply spray plus -er, the thing that makes spray, so anchor it in the tool itself.
normalIntro.cn: sprayer 就是 spray 加 -er，表示「制造喷雾的东西」，抓住器具画面来记。

normal.en: A sprayer is the device, spray is the mist, and spraying is the action.
normal.cn: sprayer 是器具，spray 是细雾，spraying 是动作。

normal.en: Gardeners use a sprayer on roses and vegetables.
normal.cn: 园丁用喷壶给月季和蔬菜喷药。

normal.en: Farm sprayers mount on tractors and carry chemical tanks.
normal.cn: 农用喷药机装在拖拉机上，拖着药箱。

normal.en: A paint sprayer coats fences faster than a brush.
normal.cn: 喷漆机刷栅栏比刷子快得多。

normal.en: Compare sprinkler: a sprinkler drops water on grass, while a sprayer sends fine mist on leaves or surfaces.
normal.cn: 对比 sprinkler：sprinkler 往草地上洒水，sprayer 则把细雾喷到叶片或表面上。

abstract.en: Picture a finger squeezing a trigger until mist blooms out.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指扣下扳机，雾一下绽开。

abstract.en: Picture dew dots of spray settling on a single leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象细小的雾点在单片叶子上凝成水珠。

abstract.en: Picture a big tank riding on a tractor over even rows.
abstract.cn: 想象一个大水箱随拖拉机驶过整齐的田垄。

examples.en: The sprayer needs cleaning after every use.
examples.cn: 每次用完后喷雾器都要清洗。

examples.en: Farmers hired a specialist to service the sprayer.
examples.cn: 农民请了专业人员来检修喷药机。

examples.en: A small hose sprayer is enough for the balcony plants.
examples.cn: 对于阳台上的植物，一只软管喷水器就够了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘶不雷」——一按就「嘶」地冒雾，散得又细又不「雷」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中古荷兰语 sprayen（洒、溅）→ 英语 spray（喷洒）→ 加工具后缀 -er → sprayer（喷雾器、喷洒器）；spray 的更早来源一般认为在中古荷兰语。

sensesIntro.en: Sprayer always names the tool that sprays, branching from the household device to farm machines, industry units, and the workers who run them.
sensesIntro.cn: sprayer 始终指「会喷的器具」，从家用喷壶分叉到农用机器、工业设备与操作工人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand-held bottle turning liquid into fine mist.
core.cn: 核心意象：手压喷壶把液体变成细雾。

branches.en: The general household device is the first sense.
branches.cn: 通用家用喷壶是第一个义项。

branches.en: Farm machinery is the biggest, most industrial version.
branches.cn: 农用机器是最大、最工业化的版本。

branches.en: Painting and washing units are the trade tools.
branches.cn: 喷漆与清洗装置是行业工具。

branches.en: The worker who runs the device is the human reading of -er.
branches.cn: 操作设备的人是这个工具后缀的人称读法。

branches.en: Medical and cosmetic mist units are the smallest versions.
branches.cn: 医疗与化妆品细雾装置是最小的版本。

intro.en: Sprayer is built from the free word spray plus the suffix -er, which names the thing doing the action.
intro.cn: sprayer 由自由词 spray 加后缀 -er 构成，-er 用来指做这件事的东西。

latinIntro.en: Spray is not Latin in origin, but the suffix -er echoes Latin agent endings.
latinIntro.cn: spray 并非拉丁来源，但后缀 -er 在功能上呼应拉丁语的施事词尾。

items.example: Please spray the plants once a week.
items.exampleCN: 请每周给这些植物喷一次水。

items.example: The sprayer hums when the trigger is held.
items.exampleCN: 按住扳机时喷雾器嗡嗡作响。

items.meaningCN: 表示做某事的人或工具
items.example: The suffix -er forms tool nouns like sprayer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 sprayer 这类工具名词。

items.example: Spraying should wait for calm weather.
items.exampleCN: 喷洒要等天风平浪静时进行。

items.example: The new coating is sprayable and cheap.
items.exampleCN: 这种新涂料能喷，还便宜。

items.example: The sprayman checked his mask first.
items.exampleCN: 喷药工先检查了口罩。

items.example: Latin agent endings carry the same idea.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语的施事词尾表达同样的想法。

items.example: The spray gun sped up the painting.
items.exampleCN: 喷枪加快了刷漆速度。

items.example: The suffix -able forms sprayable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 sprayable。

definition_zh: 发芽；长出；嫩芽；苗；涌现出；萌生
definition_en: to begin to grow as a plant, or a young shoot that has just grown from a seed
core_image: 一粒种子顶破土皮，冒出两片小小的绿叶
scene: 春天一到，院子里埋下的豆子纷纷冒头。In spring, the beans we planted in the garden finally sprout.
sceneCN: 这里 sprout 是「发芽」（第 1 个义项：种子长出芽和茎叶）；句意：春天一到，我们种在园子里的豆子终于发芽了。

pos.zh: 发芽；长出；冒出；开始生长

derivatives.zh: 由 sprout 加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「发芽的；长芽的」
由 sprout 加 -ing 构成的名词，义为「发芽；萌芽过程」

senses.title: To begin to grow as a plant
senses.definition: to start growing, pushing a stem and small leaves out of a seed or a root
senses.definitionCN: 开始生长，从种子或根部顶出茎和嫩叶
senses.example: The radish seeds sprout within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 萝卜籽一周之内就会发芽。
senses.why: The verb comes from the noun for a new shoot, so to sprout is to produce that shoot and break through the soil.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词源自表示「新芽」的名词，所以发芽就是长出那根新芽并破土而出。

senses.title: A young shoot of a plant
senses.definition: a small tender shoot, stem, or leaf that has just come from a seed or a root
senses.definitionCN: 刚从种子或根部长出的细小茎叶
senses.example: A green sprout appeared beside the step.
senses.exampleCN: 台阶旁边冒出了一根嫩绿的小苗。
senses.why: The noun names the concrete thing that the action produces, the first visible sign of a new plant.
senses.whyCN: 名词义指动作产生的那件具体东西，也就是新植物第一个看得见的迹象。

senses.title: A bean or seed eaten as a vegetable
senses.definition: a bean or seed, especially a mung or soy bean, grown briefly in water and eaten as a vegetable
senses.definitionCN: 在水中短时间催发后当蔬菜吃的豆子，尤指绿豆或黄豆
senses.example: She added a handful of fresh bean sprouts to the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她往汤里加了一把新鲜的豆芽。
senses.why: Sprouts were once only the young shoots of garden plants, then the word narrowed onto the common edible ones sold as food.
senses.whyCN: 嫩芽原来只指园子里植物的幼茎，后来词义收窄到常吃的、作为食材出售的那几种。

senses.title: Ears or horns pushing out
senses.definition: to grow or make something grow outwards, such as ears or a new part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 向上、向外生出某物，如耳朵或身体的新部分
senses.example: The lamb is already sprouting a pair of small horns.
senses.exampleCN: 这只小羊已经长出两只小角了。
senses.why: The image is extended from plants to any body part that breaks out from the surface, still keeping the idea of new growth.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象从植物扩展到任何从表面冒出来的身体部位，依然保留「新长出来」的意思。

senses.title: To appear very quickly in large numbers
senses.definition: to appear suddenly and in large numbers, often used of buildings, shops, or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 突然、大量地出现，常用于建筑、商店或想法
senses.example: New coffee shops sprout up along the old street every month.
senses.exampleCN: 老街上每个月都冒出新的咖啡馆。
senses.why: Like shoots after rain, things that sprout seem to push up from nowhere, so the word describes rapid, clustered growth.
senses.whyCN: 像雨后的春笋一样，所谓「冒出」的东西仿佛从天而降，于是这个词用来形容快速、成片地增长。

senses.title: An idea that begins to grow
senses.definition: to begin to exist and grow, used of ideas, hopes, or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 指想法、希望或感情开始出现并生长
senses.example: The hope of moving abroad sprouted in his mind.
senses.exampleCN: 出国的念头在他脑中萌生了。
senses.why: A thought has a seed and a shoot, so people say it sprouts rather than merely starts, capturing quiet organic growth.
senses.whyCN: 一个念头有种子也有幼苗，所以说它「萌生」而不只是「开始」，能抓住那种安静的、自然生长感。

intro.en: Sprout is a native English plant word; it comes from Old English sprutan, meaning to sprout or shoot forth, and is related to sprout as a shoot.
intro.cn: sprout 是英语本族语的植物词，来自古英语 sprutan（发芽、冒出），与表示「新芽」的名词同源。

items.en: Sprutan means to sprout or shoot forth, and appears in early plant descriptions.
items.cn: 古英语 sprutan 表示发芽、向外冒出，出现在早期植物描写里。

items.en: A related noun joins the image of a new shoot coming out of the ground.
items.cn: 相关的名词形式把「新芽出土」的画面固定下来。

items.en: Sprout is used for the edible young shoots of common garden beans.
items.cn: sprout 被用来指常见园栽豆类可食用的嫩茎。

items.en: The noun also names sudden growth of houses and crowds in old descriptions of towns.
items.cn: 名词还用来描述城镇里房屋和人群的骤然增多。

items.en: Sprout covers bean sprouts on a menu and new shops that pop up around a corner.
items.cn: 现代英语里，sprout 既指菜单上的豆芽，也指街角不断冒出的新店铺。

items.en: The idea of growth is applied to hopes and plans that quietly begin to exist.
items.cn: 「生长」的意象进一步用于悄然出现的希望与计划。

note.en: Sprout is a native plant word, close in form to spout and sprout words, and near in meaning to shoot, bud, and germinate.
note.cn: sprout 是英语本族语的植物词，形式上与 spout 等词相邻，意义上与 shoot、bud、germinate 接近。

normalIntro.en: Sprout sounds like spring plus out: something small pushes out of the ground in spring.
normalIntro.cn: sprout 让人想到 spring 加 out：春天的东西从地里冒出来。

normal.en: Sprout keeps the old English sense of shooting forth.
normal.cn: sprout 保留了古英语「向外冒出」的含义。

normal.en: Bean sprouts are sold by the bag in most markets.
normal.cn: 大多数市场里豆芽是整袋卖的。

normal.en: Remember sprout up for new shops and houses.
normal.cn: 记住 sprout up 可用来说新开的店、新盖的房子。

normal.en: A sprouting seed is the first sign of a new plant.
normal.cn: 正在发芽的种子是新植物最初的迹象。

normal.en: Compare shoot: a shoot is visible above ground, a sprout is often the first push through soil.
normal.cn: 对比 shoot：shoot 是在地上看得见的嫩枝，sprout 常指出土的第一下。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny green point cracking the soil surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小小的绿尖顶破了土面。

abstract.en: Imagine two fresh leaves unfolding above a bean.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗豆子上方展开两片新叶。

abstract.en: Think of rows of white bean sprouts in a paper bag.
abstract.cn: 想一想纸袋里一排排白嫩的豆芽。

examples.en: Seeds kept in a dry drawer will not sprout.
examples.cn: 放在干燥抽屉里的种子不会发芽。

examples.en: Rows of small shops sprouted up after the station opened.
examples.cn: 车站开通后，一排排小店很快冒了出来。

examples.en: She topped the noodles with handfuls of mung bean sprouts.
examples.cn: 她在面条上撒了几把绿豆芽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死跑出」——种子憋不住，拼命跑出地面冒出芽；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 sprutan（发芽、向外冒出）→ 中古英语 sprout（嫩芽；冒出来）→ 现代英语 sprout（发芽；豆芽；涌现）；核心义「从土里顶出去」，与 sprout 的名词义同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Sprout starts with a plant breaking through soil, then names the shoot, narrows to the edible sprouts, and finally spreads to things and ideas that quickly push up.
sensesIntro.cn: sprout 先从植物破土发芽说起，再指那根嫩芽，收窄到可食用的豆芽，最后扩展到快速冒出来的事物和念头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bean cracking the soil, with two small leaves rising.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗豆子顶破土层，两片小叶子升起来。

branches.en: The action of a seed pushing a shoot upward.
branches.cn: 种子顶出新芽的动作。

branches.en: The concrete shoot itself is the second sense.
branches.cn: 那根具体的嫩芽就是第二个义项。

branches.en: The edible bean sprouts are a narrowed food sense.
branches.cn: 可食用的豆芽是收窄后的食物义项。

branches.en: Body parts that push out, like ears and horns, repeat the plant image.
branches.cn: 耳朵、角这类向外长出的部位重复了植物的画面。

branches.en: Shops and ideas both seem to push up from nowhere.
branches.cn: 店铺和念头都像是凭空冒出来的。

intro.en: Sprout is a native Germanic word with almost no Latin relatives; its family grows through the English inflections and compounds bean sprout and sprout up.
intro.cn: sprout 是日耳曼语本族词，几乎没有拉丁同源词；它的词族主要通过英语的屈折变化，以及 bean sprout、sprout up 等组合扩展。

latinIntro.en: Sprout has no Latin source; it belongs to the Germanic stock of English, so there are no Latin cognates to list.
latinIntro.cn: sprout 没有拉丁语来源，它属于英语的日耳曼语层，因此没有可列的拉丁同源词。

items.exampleCN: sprutan 是有记录的最早祖先形式。

items.example: Sprout now means to start growing.
items.exampleCN: 现在 sprout 表示开始生长。

items.example: A sprout is a small new shoot.
items.exampleCN: sprout 指刚长出的小芽。

items.example: The seed sprouts in the sun.
items.exampleCN: 种子在阳光下发芽。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾
items.example: The beans sprouted overnight.
items.exampleCN: 豆子一夜之间就发芽了。

items.example: The sprouting stage lasts a few days.
items.exampleCN: 发芽阶段持续几天。

items.example: Add bean sprouts at the end of cooking.
items.exampleCN: 快出锅时加入豆芽。

items.meaning: to appear quickly in large numbers
items.example: New stalls sprout up near the market.
items.exampleCN: 市场附近很快冒出许多新摊位。

items.example: Keep the sprouting seeds damp.
items.exampleCN: 让正在发芽的种子保持湿润。

items.example: Sprouted grain is easier to digest.
items.exampleCN: 发芽的谷物更容易消化。

definition_zh: 勇敢的；有胆量的；精神饱满的；有干劲的；有活力的
definition_en: brave, determined, and full of energy, especially in a way that people admire
core_image: 一个小个子昂着头站出来，眼里带着火花
scene: 球队落后时队长仍然奔跑呐喊。The captain stayed spunky even when the team was three goals behind.
sceneCN: 这里 spunky 是「勇敢的；有胆量的」（第 1 个义项：不因困难而退缩）；句意：即使球队落后三球，队长依然斗志昂扬。

pos.zh: 勇敢的；有胆量的；有干劲的

collocations.zh: 勇敢的小孩；有主见的孩子

derivatives.zh: spunky 去掉后缀 -y 得到的名词，义为「勇气；胆量；干劲」
由 spunky 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「勇敢地；有干劲地」
由 spunky 加 -ness 构成的名词，义为「胆量；冲劲」

senses.title: Brave and not easily frightened
senses.definition: showing courage and not giving in when things are difficult or frightening
senses.definitionCN: 在困难或可怕的情况下表现勇气、不退缩
senses.example: The spunky little girl refused to leave her dog alone.
senses.exampleCN: 那个勇敢的小姑娘不肯把狗单独留下。
senses.why: The old word spunk meant a spark or a lively spirit, so a spunky person is one whose inner fire will not be put out.
senses.whyCN: 古词 spunk 意为「火星、活气」，所以 spunky 指内心那把火熄不掉的人。

senses.title: Full of energy and high spirits
senses.definition: lively, energetic, and cheerful in the way one moves and talks
senses.definitionCN: 行动和说话时都很有活力、兴致高昂
senses.example: Their spunky lead singer kept the crowd dancing all night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们那位活力四射的主唱让全场跳了一整夜。
senses.why: Since spunk was once a name for the vital force in the body, spunky came to mean full of that force.
senses.whyCN: spunk 曾经指体内的生命力，于是 spunky 就表示满身这股劲。

senses.title: Plucky and full of initiative
senses.definition: showing determination and initiative, especially in a small business or a young person
senses.definitionCN: 表现出决心与主动性，尤指小企业或年轻人
senses.example: A spunky local bakery outlasted three big chains on the same street.
senses.exampleCN: 一家有闯劲的本地面包店在同一条街上熬过了三家大型连锁。
senses.why: Bravery in danger and drive in work share the same inner spark, so the word also praises bold enterprise.
senses.whyCN: 面对危险的勇气和工作中的干劲是同一簇内在火星，所以这个词也用来称赞敢闯敢干。

senses.title: Bold to the point of being cheeky
senses.definition: bold, lively, and slightly impolite, used with mild disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 大胆、活泼而有点失礼，带轻微不赞成的意味
senses.example: That was a spunky answer to give the principal.
senses.exampleCN: 对着校长这样回话，可真是够冒失的。
senses.why: Too much spirit can tip over into cheek, so the word sometimes carries a mild warning rather than praise.
senses.whyCN: 劲头过头就会变成没规矩，所以这个词有时是轻微提醒，而不是夸奖。

senses.title: Spirited and feisty, of a story character
senses.definition: describing a fictional character who is lively, bold, and refuses to be quiet or obedient
senses.definitionCN: 形容虚构人物活泼大胆，不肯顺从或沉默
senses.example: Critics loved the spunky heroine who argues with everyone and wins.
senses.exampleCN: 评论界很喜欢那个跟谁都能吵、而且总能赢的泼辣女主角。
senses.why: Fiction uses spunky for characters who carry the spark of life into every scene they walk into.
senses.whyCN: 文学里用 spunky 形容那些走进每个场景都带着生命火星的角色。

intro.en: Spunky comes from spunk, an older Scottish and Irish word for a spark or tinder, later for spirit or courage.
intro.cn: spunky 源自 spunk，这是苏格兰与爱尔兰较早的词，指火星或引火绒，后来指精神、胆量。

items.en: Spunk first names a spark, tinder, or the spongy wood used to start a fire.
items.cn: spunk 最早指火星、引火绒，或用来生火的松软木头。

items.en: From the fire image, spunk comes to mean spirit, pluck, and courage.
items.cn: 从火的意象出发，spunk 逐渐表示精神、胆量和勇气。

items.en: Spunky is formed from spunk with the adjective suffix y.
items.cn: spunky 由 spunk 加形容词后缀 y 构成。

items.en: Spunky describes plucky, high spirited people, especially children and small animals.
items.cn: spunky 用来形容大胆、有精神的人，尤指小孩和小动物。

items.en: Informal American use adds lively and bold small businesses and young companies.
items.cn: 二十世纪美式口语用法又把它扩展到有声有势的小店与年轻公司。

items.en: The word is now mostly approving, but can still sound slightly cheeky in some contexts.
items.cn: 现在这个词多数是褒义，但在某些语境里仍会带一点冒失的味道。

note.en: Spunky is built on spunk, and it sits close to plucky and feisty in meaning while looking like other y adjectives.
note.cn: spunky 建立在 spunk 之上，意义上与 plucky、feisty 接近，形式上则和其他以 y 结尾的形容词相似。

entries.definitionCN: 海绵。只是拼写相近，词源不同

brave in a difficult situation

normalIntro.en: Spunky is spunk plus the adjective ending y, so it means full of spunk, that is, full of spark.
normalIntro.cn: spunky 是 spunk 加形容词词尾 y，意为满身都是 spunk，也就是满是火星。

normal.en: Spunk once meant tinder, the stuff that catches fire.
normal.cn: spunk 曾指引火绒，就是最容易着火的东西。

normal.en: Keep the base word spunk to remember the spirit sense.
normal.cn: 记住基础词 spunk 就记住了「精神、胆量」这层意思。

normal.en: Spunky kid is the most common everyday phrase.
normal.cn: a spunky kid 是最常见的日常说法。

normal.en: The adjective spunky gives the adverb spunkily and the noun spunkiness.
normal.cn: 副词形式是 spunkily，名词形式是 spunkiness。

normal.en: Compare plucky: both mean brave, but spunky adds energy and liveliness.
normal.cn: 对比 plucky：两者都表示勇敢，但 spunky 更强调活力与精神头。

abstract.en: Picture a match flaring up inside someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人体内有一根火柴被划亮。

abstract.en: See a small person stepping forward with a bright grin.
abstract.cn: 看到一个身材小的人带着灿烂的笑往前迈步。

abstract.en: Think of a scrappy dog pulling a cart uphill.
abstract.cn: 想象一只不服输的小狗拉着车上坡。

examples.en: It was spunky of her to speak first at the meeting.
examples.cn: 她在会上第一个发言，很有胆量。

examples.en: The spunky puppy kept chasing its own tail for an hour.
examples.cn: 那只活蹦乱跳的小狗追着自己的尾巴跑了一个小时。

examples.en: A spunky new app beat three larger rivals to the prize.
examples.cn: 一款很有闯劲的新应用击败三家更大的对手夺冠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「散朋克」——一群散开的朋克乐迷，个个都特立独行、天不怕地不怕；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 苏格兰语 spunk（火星；引火绒；活力）→ 十八世纪引申为「精神、胆量」→ 英语 spunky（胆大而精神饱满的）；核心义「体内那把火」，与 spunk 同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Spunky moves from brave in danger, to lively in spirits, to enterprising at work, and finally to mildly cheeky and to the feisty fictional heroine.
sensesIntro.cn: spunky 从危难中的勇敢，转到精神饱满，再到工作中的闯劲，最后延伸到略带冒失和无拘无束的小说女主角。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small figure standing up straight with a spark in the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小个子挺直身子站着，眼里闪着火星。

branches.en: Courage is the most basic sense, fire that will not go out.
branches.cn: 勇气是最基本的义项，是熄不掉的火。

branches.en: High spirits come straight from the vital force sense of spunk.
branches.cn: 精神饱满直接来自 spunk 的「生命力」义。

branches.en: Enterprising shops and young people carry the same spark into work.
branches.cn: 敢闯的小店和年轻人把同一簇火星带进了工作。

branches.en: A little too much fire becomes cheek rather than courage.
branches.cn: 火气过盛就从勇气变成了冒犯。

branches.en: Lively heroines in fiction keep the spirited sense alive.
branches.cn: 小说里活泼的女主角让「精神头」这一义项延续下来。

intro.en: Spunky is spunk plus the English adjective suffix y; the base word is Scottish and Irish rather than Latin.
intro.cn: spunky 是 spunk 加英语形容词后缀 y 构成的，基词来自苏格兰与爱尔兰语，而非拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for spunk; the suffix y of spunky has a Germanic origin and only adds the sense of having a quality.
latinIntro.cn: spunk 没有拉丁语祖先；spunky 的后缀 y 源自日耳曼语，只表示「具有某种性质」。

items.example: Spunk first meant tinder for a fire.
items.exampleCN: spunk 最早指生火用的引火绒。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y turns spunk into spunky.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 把 spunk 变成 spunky。

items.example: Spunky describes a lively, brave person.
items.exampleCN: spunky 形容勇敢又有精神的人。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb spunkily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 spunkily。

items.example: She answered spunkily and stood her ground.
items.exampleCN: 她大胆地回答，寸步不让。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms the noun spunkiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成名词 spunkiness。

items.example: Her spunkiness won the whole class over.
items.exampleCN: 她的冲劲赢得了全班人的心。

items.example: The younger one is the spunkiest of the three.
items.exampleCN: 三只当中最小的那只最有劲。

items.example: The back row looked spunkier after halftime.
items.exampleCN: 中场休息后，后排队员看起来更有劲头了。

items.example: The spunkiest volunteer took the hardest job.
items.exampleCN: 最有干劲的志愿者挑下了最难的活。

items.example: The team showed real spunk in the last minute.
items.exampleCN: 球队在最后一分钟展现了真正的拼劲。
